2	
3	    uv run python -m unittest test_gate -v

5	Every test builds a small vault and a git repository in a temporary directory, so nothing here
6	touches the factory's own docs/ or tags. The interface under test is the seed's Goal:
7	gate.main(argv, root) shaped like builder.main, argv[0] the program name; problems on stdout, one
8	per line, each starting with the path relative to root; exit 1 when there is any, 0 and silence
9	when there is none; usage on stderr and exit 2 for a missing or unknown command.
10	"""

23	IDENTITY = {
24	    "GIT_AUTHOR_NAME": "t",

26	    "GIT_COMMITTER_NAME": "t",

31	def fm(**fields) -> str:
32	    """Frontmatter as the vault writes it: `key: value`, `key:` when the value is empty."""
33	    return "---\n" + "".join(f"{k}: {v}\n" if str(v) else f"{k}:\n" for k, v in fields.items()) + "---\n"
34	
35	
36	TEMPLATE_SEED = fm(type="seed", status="open", summary="", value="", effort="", version="") + "\n## Evidence\n\n## Idea\n"
37	TEMPLATE_VERSION = fm(type="version") + "\n# v0.0: name\n\nWhat the version is for.\n\n## Changelog\n\n-\n"
38	BASE = 'filters:\n  and:\n    - type == "seed"\nviews:\n  - type: table\n    name: Specs\n'
39	SEED_A = fm(type="seed", status="open", summary="an idea", value=3, effort="S", version="") + (
40	    "\n## Evidence\n\nRun x, 2026-09-16.\n\n## Idea\n\nDo y, see [[b]].\n"
41	)
42	SEED_B = fm(type="seed", status="spec", summary="a spec", value=4, effort="M", version="v0.2") + (
43	    "\n## Evidence\n\nRun y, 2026-09-16.\n\n## Goal\n\nAdd z so that w.\n"
44	)
45	SEED_D = fm(type="seed", status="done", summary="delivered", value=5, effort="S", version="v0.1") + (
46	    "\n## Evidence\n\nRun z, 2026-09-15.\n\n## Goal\n\nThe first thing.\n"
47	)
48	V01 = fm(type="version") + (
49	    "\n# v0.1: the start\n\nThe first version did the first thing.\n\n"
50	    "## Changelog\n\n- The first thing, done.\n- The second thing, done.\n\n## Runs\n\nNone kept.\n"
51	)
52	V02 = fm(type="version") + (
53	    "\n# v0.2: the next\n\nThe next version does the next thing.\n\n![[backlog.base#Specs]]\n\n"
54	    "## Changelog\n\n- The next thing, built.\n"
55	)

57	TEST_GREEN = '''\
58	import unittest
59	
60	
61	class WorldTest(unittest.TestCase):
62	    def test_d(self):
63	        """seed: d. The first thing holds."""
64	        self.assertEqual(1, 1)
65	'''
66	TEST_GREEN_B = TEST_GREEN + '''
67	    def test_b(self):
68	        """seed: b. The next thing holds."""
69	        self.assertEqual(2, 2)
70	'''

78	def git(root: Path, *args: str) -> str:
79	    return subprocess.run(["git", *args], cwd=root, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout
80	
81	
82	def write(root: Path, rel: str, text: str) -> None:
83	    path = root / rel
84	    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
85	    path.write_text(text)
86

88	def make_repo(base: Path) -> Path:
89	    """A valid repository: v0.1 tagged with seed d done, v0.2 in flight with seed b at spec."""
90	    root = base / "repo"
91	    write(root, "docs/templates/seed.md", TEMPLATE_SEED)
92	    write(root, "docs/templates/version.md", TEMPLATE_VERSION)
93	    write(root, "docs/backlog.base", BASE)
94	    write(root, "docs/seeds/a.md", SEED_A)
95	    write(root, "docs/seeds/b.md", SEED_B)
96	    write(root, "docs/seeds/d.md", SEED_D)
97	    write(root, "docs/versions/v0.1.md", V01)
98	    write(root, "docs/versions/v0.2.md", V02)
99	    write(root, "AGENTS.md", AGENTS)
100	    write(root, "test_world.py", TEST_GREEN)
101	    write(root, ".gitignore", "__pycache__/\n")
102	    git(root, "init", "-q")
103	    git(root, "add", "-A")
104	    git(root, "commit", "-q", "-m", "one")
105	    git(root, "tag", "v0.1")
106	    return root
107	
108	
109	def run(root: Path, *args: str) -> tuple[int, str, str]:
110	    out, err = io.StringIO(), io.StringIO()
111	    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(out), contextlib.redirect_stderr(err):
112	        code = gate.main(["gate.py", *args], root=root)
113	    return code, out.getvalue(), err.getvalue()

116	class GateTest(unittest.TestCase):
117	    def setUp(self):
118	        self.tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
119	        self.addCleanup(self.tmp.cleanup)
120	        self.enterContext(mock.patch.dict(os.environ, IDENTITY))
121	        self.root = make_repo(Path(self.tmp.name))
122	
123	    def edit(self, rel: str, text: str) -> None:
124	        write(self.root, rel, text)
125	
126	    def commit(self, message: str = "more") -> None:
127	        git(self.root, "add", "-A")
128	        git(self.root, "commit", "-q", "-m", message)
129	
130	    def check(self) -> tuple[int, str, str]:
131	        return run(self.root, "check")
132	
133	    def assert_problem(self, *words: str) -> str:
134	        code, out, err = self.check()
135	        self.assertEqual(code, 1, out)
136	        for word in words:
137	            self.assertIn(word, out)
138	        return out

3	The factory is `builder.py`: a program that runs a cold model session over a directory, the world, until the world's tests pass, under walls the model cannot cross. It is built one version at a time and its own repository is its first world. Since v0.3 the code is written by `builder.py` itself, from tests written before it runs; the first change it built is commit 48cbbe4. What it can do is read off the records of its runs. Nothing in this repository is written for a model to obey; what holds is held by tests, by the plane and by git.
4	
5	You are the attended agent: a model in some harness, resuming this work cold, working with the owner. This file is for any such model. The state of the work is never narrated here; it is derived from git and the files, as below.
6	
7	## Orient yourself
8	
9	Run these before reading anything else, from the root of the checkout or worktree you are in:
10	
11	```sh
12	uv run python -m unittest -q                                       # the factory's tests; no provider, no network, no docker
13	git tag -l --format='%(refname:strip=2) %(objectname:short)'       # the released versions
14	git log --oneline "tags/$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD"   # what happened since the last one
15	git status --short                                                 # what is not committed; see the last section
16	ls docs/versions docs/seeds                                        # the versions and the backlog
17	ls "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/../runs" | tail -3           # the last run records; see the last section
18	```
19	
20	Then derive:
21	
22	- The version in flight is the note in `docs/versions/` whose name is not a tag. Its seeds are the notes in `docs/seeds/` whose `version` names it.
23	- A seed's stage is its `status`. `open`: evidence and an idea. `spec`: a `## Goal` the builder can be given, assigned to a version. `building`: at least one test names it, `seed: <name>` in the test's docstring, committed red. `done`: merged and green. `docs/templates/seed.md` states what each status requires; `docs/backlog.base` ranks the seeds.
24	- What the builder does and refuses is `README.md`; the walls are the constants at the top of `builder.py`; the exact behaviour is `test_builder.py`.
25	- A run is a directory under `runs/`: read `numbers.json` first (`stopped`, `check`, cost, counts), then `response.md`, `diff.patch` and `wire.jsonl`.
26	
27	## How a version is made
28	
29	The owner and the attended agent choose seeds from the backlog and promote them to specs: a version is assigned, the idea becomes a goal. For each spec the attended agent writes the tests that name the seed, commits them red on a branch in a git worktree, and runs `builder.py` on that worktree with the seed's goal. The factory writes the code. The attended agent reads the record and the diff, commits the diff as the factory's work, merges it, and tags the merge with the version; the version note holds the changelog. The attended agent does not write code the factory could write and does not touch a test to make a build pass, because the factory's ability to do it is what is being measured; the plane refuses the model the same. Tags are plain until seed `the-gate` lands; the gate cuts them annotated with the changelog and renders `CHANGELOG.md`.
30	
31	## Commands
32	
33	- `uv run python -m unittest -v`: the factory's own tests. Nothing external is needed.
34	- `uv run builder.py <world> "<goal>"`: one build. Needs the DeepSeek key in `~/.config/factory/deepseek.key` and docker, since the check runs in a container built once from the world's `uv.lock` and `check.Dockerfile`. Leaves `runs/<utc-stamp>/` beside the `builder.py` that ran, never in the world: run it from the main checkout and pass the worktree as the world. Exits 0 when the model returned a report, 1 on a cap or a provider error, 2 on a usage error. The cost and the time are in the record.
35	- `git worktree add <path> -b <branch>`: a world for a build. `.claude/worktrees/` is an ignored place for one.
36	- `git push origin main --tags`: the mirror is `git@github-joam:yellow-robots/factory.git`. `github-joam` is an SSH alias on this host that selects the owner's key; two GitHub identities share the machine.
37	
38	## Not derivable from the repository
39	
40	- `docs/` is an Obsidian vault the owner keeps open. Obsidian rewrites a file it shows: frontmatter reordered, a `{{...}}` in the frontmatter destroyed, a `.base` file reformatted. A dirty `docs/` may be the owner's content or Obsidian's rewrite; read the diff before committing or discarding it.
41	- A version exists only as a tag. Commit 48cbbe4 is titled `v0.4` and belongs to no version.
42	- Branches `bootstrap` and `v0.1` to `v0.4` are leftovers of past worktrees; `v0.1` to `v0.3` share their names with the tags, so git warns and prefers the tag. Write `tags/v0.3` where it matters.
43	- `runs/` and `plans/` are ignored. The records exist in the main checkout on this host only, until seed `commit-the-runs` lands. `plans/` is scratch for plan files; the plans of v0.2 and v0.3 are appended to their version notes.
44	- The model is DeepSeek `deepseek-flash`. pydantic-ai does not know the name, so `builder.py` carries a profile override; genai-prices has no row for it, so the price table in `builder.py` is the cost source. Thinking is on by default and ignores temperature. The key is never printed or committed.
45	- The history before this repository, v1 and the design that was abandoned for it, is in the owner's Obsidian vault at `/srv/obsidian/vaults/obsidian/03 archive/factory-v1/`. Reference, never a plan.

3	The factory is `builder.py`: a program that runs a cold model session over a directory, the world, until the world's tests pass, under walls the model cannot cross. 7	## Orient yourself
8	
9	Run these before reading anything else, from the root of the checkout or worktree you are in:

21	
22	- The version in flight is the note in `docs/versions/` whose name is not a tag. Its seeds are the notes in `docs/seeds/` whose `version` names it.
23	- A seed's stage is its `status`. `open`: evidence and an idea. `spec`: a `## Goal` the builder can be given, assigned to a version. `building`: at least one test names it, `seed: <name>` in the test's docstring, committed red. `done`: merged and green. `docs/templates/seed.md` states what each status requires; `docs/backlog.base` ranks the seeds.
24	- What the builder does and refuses is `README.md`; the walls are the constants at the top of `builder.py`; the exact behaviour is `test_builder.py`.
25	- A run is a directory under `runs/`: read `numbers.json` first (`stopped`, `check`, cost, counts), then `response.md`, `diff.patch` and `wire.jsonl`.
26	
27	## How a version is made
28	
29	The owner and the attended agent choose seeds from the backlog and promote them to specs: a version is assigned, the idea becomes a goal. For each spec the attended agent writes the tests that name the seed, commits them red on a branch in a git worktree, and runs `builder.py` on that worktree with the seed's goal. The factory writes the code. The attended agent reads the record and the diff, commits the diff as the factory's work, merges it, and tags the merge with the version; the version note holds the changelog. The attended agent does not write code the factory could write and does not touch a test to make a build pass, because the factory's ability to do it is what is being measured; the plane refuses the model the same. Tags are plain until seed `the-gate` lands; the gate cuts them annotated with the changelog and renders `CHANGELOG.md`.

32	
33	- `uv run python -m unittest -v`: the factory's own tests. Nothing external is needed.
34	- `uv run builder.py <world> "<goal>"`: one build. Leaves `runs/<utc-stamp>/` beside the `builder.py` that ran, never in the world: run it from the main checkout and pass the worktree as the world. `final_result` function: changed (the paths you wrote or edited, in order), did (what you
changed and why, one fact per item, each naming a path), check (green or red), failing (test
names if red), unsure (what you could not determine or verify).

3	The factory is `builder.py`: a program that runs a cold model session over a directory, the world, until the world's tests pass, under walls the model cannot cross. Nothing in this repository is written for a model to obey; what holds is held by tests, by the plane and by git.

5	You are the attended agent: a model in some harness, resuming this work cold, working with the owner. This file is for any such model. The state of the work is never narrated here; it is derived from git and the files, as below.

7	## Orient yourself
8	
9	Run these before reading anything else, from the root of the checkout or worktree you are in:

22	- The version in flight is the note in `docs/versions/` whose name is not a tag. Its seeds are the notes in `docs/seeds/` whose `version` names it.

24	- What the builder does and refuses is `README.md`; the walls are the constants at the top of `builder.py`; the exact behaviour is `test_builder.py`.

27	## How a version is made
28	
29	The owner and the attended agent choose seeds from the backlog and promote them to specs: a version is assigned, the idea becomes a goal. For each spec the attended agent writes the tests that name the seed, commits them red on a branch in a git worktree, and runs `builder.py` on that worktree with the seed's goal. The factory writes the code. The attended agent reads the record and the diff, commits the diff as the factory's work, merges it, and tags the merge with the version; the version note holds the changelog. The attended agent does not write code the factory could write and does not touch a test to make a build pass, because the factory's ability to do it is what is being measured; the plane refuses the model the same. Tags are plain until seed `the-gate` lands; the gate cuts them annotated with the changelog and renders `CHANGELOG.md`.

33	- `uv run python -m unittest -v`: the factory's own tests. Nothing external is needed.

Leaves `runs/<utc-stamp>/` beside the `builder.py` that ran, never in the world: run it from the main checkout and pass the worktree as the world. You are the builder. You are given a goal and a world: a directory with code and tests. You
can explore it with `list` and `read`, change it with `write` and `edit`, and test it with
`check`. The goal is reached when `check` is green: the tests are the goal's acceptance
criteria and cannot be changed.

Work in this order: read what the goal touches; run `check` once to see what fails; make the
smallest change that can make it pass; run `check`; repeat. Stop when `check` is green, or
when you cannot make it green within the budget, and return the report through the
`final_result` function: changed (the paths you wrote or edited, in order), did (what you
changed and why, one fact per item, each naming a path), check (green or red), failing (test
names if red), unsure (what you could not determine or verify).

Rules: change only what the goal needs; prefer `edit` over `write` for existing files; never
work around a failing test by changing what it asserts; no commentary outside the report.

2	
3	The factory is `builder.py`: a program that runs a cold model session over a directory, the world, until the world's tests pass, under walls the model cannot cross. It is built one version at a time and its own repository is its first world. Since v0.3 the code is written by `builder.py` itself, from tests written before it runs; the first change it built is commit 48cbbe4. What it can do is read off the records of its runs. Nothing in this repository is written for a model to obey; what holds is held by tests, by the plane and by git.
4	
5	You are the attended agent: a model in some harness, resuming this work cold, working with the owner. This file is for any such model. The state of the work is never narrated here; it is derived from git and the files, as below.
6	
7	## Orient yourself
8	
9	Run these before reading anything else, from the root of the checkout or worktree you are in:
10	
11	```sh
12	uv run python -m unittest -q                                       # the factory's tests; no provider, no network, no docker
13	git tag -l --format='%(refname:strip=2) %(objectname:short)'       # the released versions
14	git log --oneline "tags/$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD"   # what happened since the last one
15	git status --short                                                 # what is not committed; see the last section
16	ls docs/versions docs/seeds                                        # the versions and the backlog
17	ls "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/../runs" | tail -3           # the last run records; see the last section
18	```
19	
20	Then derive:
21	
22	- The version in flight is the note in `docs/versions/` whose name is not a tag. Its seeds are the notes in `docs/seeds/` whose `version` names it.
23	- A seed's stage is its `status`. `open`: evidence and an idea. `spec`: a `## Goal` the builder can be given, assigned to a version. `building`: at least one test names it, `seed: <name>` in the test's docstring, committed red. `done`: merged and green. `docs/templates/seed.md` states what each status requires; `docs/backlog.base` ranks the seeds.
24	- What the builder does and refuses is `README.md`; the walls are the constants at the top of `builder.py`; the exact behaviour is `test_builder.py`.
25	- A run is a directory under `runs/`: read `numbers.json` first (`stopped`, `check`, cost, counts), then `response.md`, `diff.patch` and `wire.jsonl`.
26	
27	## How a version is made
28	
29	The owner and the attended agent choose seeds from the backlog and promote them to specs: a version is assigned, the idea becomes a goal. For each spec the attended agent writes the tests that name the seed, commits them red on a branch in a git worktree, and runs `builder.py` on that worktree with the seed's goal. The factory writes the code. The attended agent reads the record and the diff, commits the diff as the factory's work, merges it, and tags the merge with the version; the version note holds the changelog. The attended agent does not write code the factory could write and does not touch a test to make a build pass, because the factory's ability to do it is what is being measured; the plane refuses the model the same. Tags are plain until seed `the-gate` lands; the gate cuts them annotated with the changelog and renders `CHANGELOG.md`.
30	
31	## Commands
32	
33	- `uv run python -m unittest -v`: the factory's own tests. Nothing external is needed.
34	- `uv run builder.py <world> "<goal>"`: one build. Needs the DeepSeek key in `~/.config/factory/deepseek.key` and docker, since the check runs in a container built once from the world's `uv.lock` and `check.Dockerfile`. Leaves `runs/<utc-stamp>/` beside the `builder.py` that ran, never in the world: run it from the main checkout and pass the worktree as the world. Exits 0 when the model returned a report, 1 on a cap or a provider error, 2 on a usage error. The cost and the time are in the record.
35	- `git worktree add <path> -b <branch>`: a world for a build. `.claude/worktrees/` is an ignored place for one.
36	- `git push origin main --tags`: the mirror is `git@github-joam:yellow-robots/factory.git`. `github-joam` is an SSH alias on this host that selects the owner's key; two GitHub identities share the machine.
37	
38	## Not derivable from the repository
39	
40	- `docs/` is an Obsidian vault the owner keeps open. Obsidian rewrites a file it shows: frontmatter reordered, a `{{...}}` in the frontmatter destroyed, a `.base` file reformatted. A dirty `docs/` may be the owner's content or Obsidian's rewrite; read the diff before committing or discarding it.
41	- A version exists only as a tag. Commit 48cbbe4 is titled `v0.4` and belongs to no version.
42	- Branches `bootstrap` and `v0.1` to `v0.4` are leftovers of past worktrees; `v0.1` to `v0.3` share their names with the tags, so git warns and prefers the tag. Write `tags/v0.3` where it matters.
43	- `runs/` and `plans/` are ignored. The records exist in the main checkout on this host only, until seed `commit-the-runs` lands. `plans/` is scratch for plan files; the plans of v0.2 and v0.3 are appended to their version notes.

Thinking is on by default and ignores temperature. The key is never printed or committed.
45	- The history before this repository, v1 and the design that was abandoned for it, is in the owner's Obsidian vault at `/srv/obsidian/vaults/obsidian/03 archive/factory-v1/`. Reference, never a plan.

10	## Evidence
11	
12	v1 kept its documents honest only with templates, a deterministic gate and hooks; every hand-maintained file without one rotted (findings report, 2026-09-12). v0.1 to v0.3 were specified in plan files outside git and closed with commit messages; nothing checked that the orientation page, the version notes and the tags agreed, and the page's first cold reader found three errors in it (commit 6cd3eca, 2026-09-16). 13	
14	## Goal
15	
16	Add `gate.py` at the repository root, run as `uv run gate.py <command>`, with `main(argv, root=None)` shaped like `builder.main`: `argv[0]` is the program name, `root` defaults to the directory `gate.py` is in. Three commands. Each prints one line per problem on stdout, starting with the path relative to `root` and saying what is missing, and exits 1 if there is any; with nothing to report it prints nothing and exits 0. A missing or unknown command, or `release` without a version, prints usage on stderr and exits 2.
17	
18	`check` validates `docs/` and the repository against it:
19	
20	- every `.md` file under `docs/`, those under `docs/templates/` excepted, has frontmatter whose `type` names a file `docs/templates/<type>.md`;
21	- every wikilink in `docs/` (a double-bracket link, with or without an alias after `|` or a heading after `#`, embedded with a leading `!` or not) resolves to a note in `docs/`, by path or by name, or to a `.base` file;
22	- a seed (`type: seed`) has `status` in open, spec, building, done, rejected, and no frontmatter field beyond type, status, summary, value, effort, version; from `open` on it has `summary`, `value` in 1 to 5 and `effort` in S, M, L; from `spec` on, `version` names a file `docs/versions/<version>.md` and the body has a `## Goal` section with text under it; from `building` on, at least one test method or class in a `test*.py` file at the repository root has a docstring containing `seed: <file name without .md>`, a comment does not count;
23	- a version note (`type: version`) has no frontmatter field beyond `type` and is named `v<major>.<minor>.md`; at most one version note is not a tag; every seed whose `version` is a tag is `done` or `rejected`.
24	
25	`render` writes `CHANGELOG.md` from the tags, newest first: for each tag, a heading from the version note's title line, the tag's date from git, then the note's first paragraph and the bullets under its `## Changelog`; embeds and the other sections stay out.
26	
27	`release <version>` refuses unless `check` passes, `docs/versions/<version>.md` exists and the tag does not, every seed carrying the version is `done` or `rejected`, the note has at least one `## Changelog` bullet, `git status --porcelain` is empty, `AGENTS.md` has changed since the previous tag (the highest existing one; no constraint when there is none), and `python -m unittest` run at `root` is green. It then creates an annotated tag `<version>` at `HEAD` whose message is the note's first paragraph and changelog bullets, and runs `render`.
28	
29	The tests naming this seed are `test_gate.py`, written before the build; every command is exercised on a temporary vault and a temporary git repository.

function.name: list
function.description:
List one directory of the world: one entry per line as kind, size, path. Path is
relative to the world root; '.' is the root.

path.description: The directory to list, relative to the world root.

function.name: read
function.description:
Read a file of the world as numbered lines, from line `start` (1-based), at most 300
lines or 32000 bytes per call; a truncated read says where to continue.

path.description: The file to read, relative to the world root.

function.name: write
function.description:
Write a file of the world: create it, or replace what is there with `content`.
Directories on the way are created. The tests and the toolchain cannot be written.

path.description: The file to write, relative to the world root.

content.description: The whole text of the file, as it should be afterwards.

function.name: edit
function.description:
Edit a file of the world: replace `old` with `new`, once. `old` must appear in the
file exactly once; if it does not, nothing is changed and the count is reported. The
tests and the toolchain cannot be edited.

path.description: The file to edit, relative to the world root.

old.description: The exact text to replace; include lines around it to make it unique.

new.description: The text to put in its place.

function.name: check
function.description:
Run the world's tests and return the exit code and the tail of the output: exit 0 is
green, anything else is red. The tests run in a container, with the world read-only and
no network, so this reports on the world as it is on disk. At most 8 checks per run.

function.name: final_result
function.description: The builder's report: what it changed in the world, and whether the tests pass.

changed.description: The paths you wrote or edited, in order.

1	# factory
2	
3	The factory is `builder.py`: a program that runs a cold model session over a directory, the world, until the world's tests pass, under walls the model cannot cross. It is built one version at a time and its own repository is its first world. Since v0.3 the code is written by `builder.py` itself, from tests written before it runs; the first change it built is commit 48cbbe4. What it can do is read off the records of its runs. Nothing in this repository is written for a model to obey; what holds is held by tests, by the plane and by git.
4	
5	You are the attended agent: a model in some harness, resuming this work cold, working with the owner. This file is for any such model. The state of the work is never narrated here; it is derived from git and the files, as below.
6	
7	## Orient yourself
8	
9	Run these before reading anything else, from the root of the checkout or worktree you are in:
10	
11	```sh
12	uv run python -m unittest -q                                       # the factory's tests; no provider, no network, no docker
13	git tag -l --format='%(refname:strip=2) %(objectname:short)'       # the released versions
14	git log --oneline "tags/$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD"   # what happened since the last one
15	git status --short                                                 # what is not committed; see the last section
16	ls docs/versions docs/seeds                                        # the versions and the backlog
17	ls "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/../runs" | tail -3           # the last run records; see the last section
18	```
19	
20	Then derive:
21	
22	- The version in flight is the note in `docs/versions/` whose name is not a tag. Its seeds are the notes in `docs/seeds/` whose `version` names it.
23	- A seed's stage is its `status`. `open`: evidence and an idea. `spec`: a `## Goal` the builder can be given, assigned to a version. `building`: at least one test names it, `seed: <name>` in the test's docstring, committed red. `done`: merged and green. `docs/templates/seed.md` states what each status requires; `docs/backlog.base` ranks the seeds.
24	- What the builder does and refuses is `README.md`; the walls are the constants at the top of `builder.py`; the exact behaviour is `test_builder.py`.
25	- A run is a directory under `runs/`: read `numbers.json` first (`stopped`, `check`, cost, counts), then `response.md`, `diff.patch` and `wire.jsonl`.
26	
27	## How a version is made
28	
29	The owner and the attended agent choose seeds from the backlog and promote them to specs: a version is assigned, the idea becomes a goal. For each spec the attended agent writes the tests that name the seed, commits them red on a branch in a git worktree, and runs `builder.py` on that worktree with the seed's goal. The factory writes the code. The attended agent reads the record and the diff, commits the diff as the factory's work, merges it, and tags the merge with the version; the version note holds the changelog. The attended agent does not write code the factory could write and does not touch a test to make a build pass, because the factory's ability to do it is what is being measured; the plane refuses the model the same. Tags are plain until seed `the-gate` lands; the gate cuts them annotated with the changelog and renders `CHANGELOG.md`.
30	
31	## Commands
32	
33	- `uv run python -m unittest -v`: the factory's own tests. Nothing external is needed.
34	- `uv run builder.py <world> "<goal>"`: one build. Needs the DeepSeek key in `~/.config/factory/deepseek.key` and docker, since the check runs in a container built once from the world's `uv.lock` and `check.Dockerfile`. Leaves `runs/<utc-stamp>/` beside the `builder.py` that ran, never in the world: run it from the main checkout and pass the worktree as the world. Exits 0 when the model returned a report, 1 on a cap or a provider error, 2 on a usage error. The cost and the time are in the record.
35	- `git worktree add <path> -b <branch>`: a world for a build. `.claude/worktrees/` is an ignored place for one.
36	- `git push origin main --tags`: the mirror is `git@github-joam:yellow-robots/factory.git`. `github-joam` is an SSH alias on this host that selects the owner's key; two GitHub identities share the machine.
37	
38	## Not derivable from the repository
39	
40	- `docs/` is an Obsidian vault the owner keeps open. Obsidian rewrites a file it shows: frontmatter reordered, a `{{...}}` in the frontmatter destroyed, a `.base` file reformatted. A dirty `docs/` may be the owner's content or Obsidian's rewrite; read the diff before committing or discarding it.
41	- A version exists only as a tag. Commit 48cbbe4 is titled `v0.4` and belongs to no version.
42	- Branches `bootstrap` and `v0.1` to `v0.4` are leftovers of past worktrees; `v0.1` to `v0.3` share their names with the tags, so git warns and prefers the tag. Write `tags/v0.3` where it matters.
43	- `runs/` and `plans/` are ignored. The records exist in the main checkout on this host only, until seed `commit-the-runs` lands. `plans/` is scratch for plan files; the plans of v0.2 and v0.3 are appended to their version notes.
44	- The model is DeepSeek `deepseek-flash`. pydantic-ai does not know the name, so `builder.py` carries a profile override; genai-prices has no row for it, so the price table in `builder.py` is the cost source. Thinking is on by default and ignores temperature. The key is never printed or committed.
45	- The history before this repository, v1 and the design that was abandoned for it, is in the owner's Obsidian vault at `/srv/obsidian/vaults/obsidian/03 archive/factory-v1/`. Reference, never a plan.

14	## Goal
15	
16	Add `gate.py` at the repository root, run as `uv run gate.py <command>`, with `main(argv, root=None)` shaped like `builder.main`: `argv[0]` is the program name, `root` defaults to the directory `gate.py` is in. Three commands. Each prints one line per problem on stdout, starting with the path relative to `root` and saying what is missing, and exits 1 if there is any; with nothing to report it prints nothing and exits 0. A missing or unknown command, or `release` without a version, prints usage on stderr and exits 2.
17	
18	`check` validates `docs/` and the repository against it:

23	- a version note (`type: version`) has no frontmatter field beyond `type` and is named `v<major>.<minor>.md`; at most one version note is not a tag; every seed whose `version` is a tag is `done` or `rejected`.

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""The builder: a cold session that changes a world until its tests pass. Factory v0.3.
3

5

7	list, read, write, edit and check. Writes are confined to the world and refused on the goal's
8	tests and the toolchain; check runs the world's tests in a container with no network and the
9	world mounted read-only, so code the model writes never runs on the host and cannot reach the
10	key. The loop is pydantic-ai, pinned; the provider is DeepSeek's chat completions API, the key
11	read from ~/.config/factory/deepseek.key and never written anywhere. Each run leaves
12	runs/<utc-stamp>/ under the factory itself, never in the world, with goal.txt, wire.jsonl (every
13	HTTP attempt as it happened), messages.json (the library's messages), check-<n>.log per check,

81	ROLE = """\
82	You are the builder. You are given a goal and a world: a directory with code and tests. You
83	can explore it with `list` and `read`, change it with `write` and `edit`, and test it with
84	`check`. The goal is reached when `check` is green: the tests are the goal's acceptance
85	criteria and cannot be changed.

88	smallest change that can make it pass; run `check`; repeat. Stop when `check` is green, or

99	class BuildReport(BaseModel):

111	SECTIONS = (("Changed", "changed"), ("Did", "did"), ("Check", "check"),
112	            ("Failing", "failing"), ("Unsure", "unsure"))  # fmt: skip

115	def render(report: BuildReport) -> str:
116	    """The report in v0.1's markdown shape: five headings, one bullet per item."""
117	    out: list[str] = []
118	    for heading, field in SECTIONS:
119	        out.append(f"## {heading}")
120	        items = getattr(report, field)
121	        if isinstance(items, str):  # check is one value, and renders as one bullet
122	            items = [items]
123	        out.extend(f"- {item}" for item in items or ["(none)"])
124	        out.append("")
125	    return "\n".join(out)

128	class Plane:
129	    """The execution plane: what the model can do to the world, and the record of it."""
130	
131	    def __init__(self, root: Path, run_dir: Path, hidden: tuple[str, ...] = HIDDEN,
132	                 protected: tuple[str, ...] = PROTECTED, sandbox: Any = None):  # fmt: skip
133	        self.root = root.resolve()
134	        self.run_dir = run_dir
135	        self.hidden = hidden
136	        self.protected = protected
137	        self.sandbox = sandbox

145	    def _resolve(self, path: str) -> tuple[Path, str]:
146	        p = (self.root / (path or ".")).resolve()
147	        if p != self.root and self.root not in p.parents:
148	            raise ValueError(f"outside the world: {path}")
149	        rel = p.relative_to(self.root).as_posix() or "."
150	        if rel.split("/", 1)[0] in self.hidden:
151	            raise ValueError(f"not part of the world: {path}")
152	        return p, rel
153	
154	    def _writable(self, rel: str) -> None:
155	        """The goal's tests and the toolchain are the human's; the builder may read them only."""
156	        name = rel.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
157	        for pattern in self.protected:
158	            if pattern.endswith("/"):  # anything under that directory
159	                hit = rel == pattern[:-1] or rel.startswith(pattern)
160	            elif "*" in pattern:  # that basename, anywhere in the world

170	    def _capped(self) -> str:
171	        if len(self.written) + len(self.edited) >= WRITE_CAP:
172	            return f"error: cap reached ({WRITE_CAP} writes and edits); report now"
173	        return ""
174	
175	    def list(self, path: str = ".") -> str:
176	        """List one directory of the world: one entry per line as kind, size, path. Path is
177	        relative to the world root; '.' is the root.

179	        Args:
180	            path: The directory to list, relative to the world root.
181	        """
182	        try:
183	            p, rel = self._resolve(path)
184	            if not p.is_dir():
185	                raise ValueError(f"not a directory: {path}")
186	            entries = sorted(p.iterdir(), key=lambda e: (not e.is_dir(), e.name))

names if red), unsure (what you could not determine or verify).

1	# factory
2	
3	The factory is `builder.py`: a program that runs a cold model session over a directory, the world, until the world's tests pass, under walls the model cannot cross. It is built one version at a time and its own repository is its first world. Since v0.3 the code is written by `builder.py` itself, from tests written before it runs; the first change it built is commit 48cbbe4. What it can do is read off the records of its runs. Nothing in this repository is written for a model to obey; what holds is held by tests, by the plane and by git.
4	
5	You are the attended agent: a model in some harness, resuming this work cold, working with the owner. This file is for any such model. The state of the work is never narrated here; it is derived from git and the files, as below.
6	
7	## Orient yourself
8	
9	Run these before reading anything else, from the root of the checkout or worktree you are in:
10	
11	```sh
12	uv run python -m unittest -q                                       # the factory's tests; no provider, no network, no docker
13	git tag -l --format='%(refname:strip=2) %(objectname:short)'       # the released versions
14	git log --oneline "tags/$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD"   # what happened since the last one
15	git status --short                                                 # what is not committed; see the last section
16	ls docs/versions docs/seeds                                        # the versions and the backlog
17	ls "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/../runs" | tail -3           # the last run records; see the last section
18	```
19	
20	Then derive:
21	
22	- The version in flight is the note in `docs/versions/` whose name is not a tag. Its seeds are the notes in `docs/seeds/` whose `version` names it.
23	- A seed's stage is its `status`. `open`: evidence and an idea. `spec`: a `## Goal` the builder can be given, assigned to a version. `building`: at least one test names it, `seed: <name>` in the test's docstring, committed red. `done`: merged and green. `docs/templates/seed.md` states what each status requires; `docs/backlog.base` ranks the seeds.
24	- What the builder does and refuses is `README.md`; the walls are the constants at the top of `builder.py`; the exact behaviour is `test_builder.py`.
25	- A run is a directory under `runs/`: read `numbers.json` first (`stopped`, `check`, cost, counts), then `response.md`, `diff.patch` and `wire.jsonl`.
26	
27	## How a version is made
28	
29	The owner and the attended agent choose seeds from the backlog and promote them to specs: a version is assigned, the idea becomes a goal. For each spec the attended agent writes the tests that name the seed, commits them red on a branch in a git worktree, and runs `builder.py` on that worktree with the seed's goal. The factory writes the code. The attended agent reads the record and the diff, commits the diff as the factory's work, merges it, and tags the merge with the version; the version note holds the changelog. The attended agent does not write code the factory could write and does not touch a test to make a build pass, because the factory's ability to do it is what is being measured; the plane refuses the model the same. Tags are plain until seed `the-gate` lands; the gate cuts them annotated with the changelog and renders `CHANGELOG.md`.
30	
31	## Commands
32	
33	- `uv run python -m unittest -v`: the factory's own tests. Nothing external is needed.
34	- `uv run builder.py <world> "<goal>"`: one build. Needs the DeepSeek key in `~/.config/factory/deepseek.key` and docker, since the check runs in a container built once from the world's `uv.lock` and `check.Dockerfile`. Leaves `runs/<utc-stamp>/` beside the `builder.py` that ran, never in the world: run it from the main checkout and pass the worktree as the world. Exits 0 when the model returned a report, 1 on a cap or a provider error, 2 on a usage error. The cost and the time are in the record.
35	- `git worktree add <path> -b <branch>`: a world for a build. `.claude/worktrees/` is an ignored place for one.
36	- `git push origin main --tags`: the mirror is `git@github-joam:yellow-robots/factory.git`. `github-joam` is an SSH alias on this host that selects the owner's key; two GitHub identities share the machine.
37	
38	## Not derivable from the repository
39	
40	- `docs/` is an Obsidian vault the owner keeps open. Obsidian rewrites a file it shows: frontmatter reordered, a `{{...}}` in the frontmatter destroyed, a `.base` file reformatted. A dirty `docs/` may be the owner's content or Obsidian's rewrite; read the diff before committing or discarding it.
41	- A version exists only as a tag. Commit 48cbbe4 is titled `v0.4` and belongs to no version.
42	- Branches `bootstrap` and `v0.1` to `v0.4` are leftovers of past worktrees; `v0.1` to `v0.3` share their names with the tags, so git warns and prefers the tag. Write `tags/v0.3` where it matters.
43	- `runs/` and `plans/` are ignored. The records exist in the main checkout on this host only, until seed `commit-the-runs` lands. `plans/` is scratch for plan files; the plans of v0.2 and v0.3 are appended to their version notes.
44	- The model is DeepSeek `deepseek-flash`. pydantic-ai does not know the name, so `builder.py` carries a profile override; genai-prices has no row for it, so the price table in `builder.py` is the cost source. Thinking is on by default and ignores temperature. The key is never printed or committed.
45	- The history before this repository, v1 and the design that was abandoned for it, is in the owner's Obsidian vault at `/srv/obsidian/vaults/obsidian/03 archive/factory-v1/`. Reference, never a plan.

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""The builder: a cold session that changes a world until its tests pass. Factory v0.3.
3	
4	    uv run builder.py <world> "<goal>"
5

7	list, read, write, edit and check. Writes are confined to the world and refused on the goal's
8	tests and the toolchain; check runs the world's tests in a container with no network and the
9	world mounted read-only, so code the model writes never runs on the host and cannot reach the
10	key. The loop is pydantic-ai, pinned; the provider is DeepSeek's chat completions API, the key
11	read from ~/.config/factory/deepseek.key and never written anywhere. Each run leaves
12	runs/<utc-stamp>/ under the factory itself, never in the world, with goal.txt, wire.jsonl (every
13	HTTP attempt as it happened), messages.json (the library's messages), check-<n>.log per check,

81	ROLE = """\
82	You are the builder. You are given a goal and a world: a directory with code and tests. You
83	can explore it with `list` and `read`, change it with `write` and `edit`, and test it with
84	`check`. The goal is reached when `check` is green: the tests are the goal's acceptance

105	    )
106	    check: Literal["green", "red"] = Field(description="Green or red: the state of the last check.")
107	    failing: list[str] = Field(description="Test names if red.")
108	    unsure: list[str] = Field(description="What you could not determine or verify.")
109

111	SECTIONS = (("Changed", "changed"), ("Did", "did"), ("Check", "check"),
112	            ("Failing", "failing"), ("Unsure", "unsure"))  # fmt: skip

115	def render(report: BuildReport) -> str:
116	    """The report in v0.1's markdown shape: five headings, one bullet per item."""
117	    out: list[str] = []
118	    for heading, field in SECTIONS:
119	        out.append(f"## {heading}")
120	        items = getattr(report, field)
121	        if isinstance(items, str):  # check is one value, and renders as one bullet
122	            items = [items]
123	        out.extend(f"- {item}" for item in items or ["(none)"])
124	        out.append("")
125	    return "\n".join(out)

128	class Plane:
129	    """The execution plane: what the model can do to the world, and the record of it."""
130	
131	    def __init__(self, root: Path, run_dir: Path, hidden: tuple[str, ...] = HIDDEN,
132	                 protected: tuple[str, ...] = PROTECTED, sandbox: Any = None):  # fmt: skip
133	        self.root = root.resolve()
134	        self.run_dir = run_dir
135	        self.hidden = hidden
136	        self.protected = protected
137	        self.sandbox = sandbox
138	        self.listed: list[str] = []

145	    def _resolve(self, path: str) -> tuple[Path, str]:
146	        p = (self.root / (path or ".")).resolve()
147	        if p != self.root and self.root not in p.parents:
148	            raise ValueError(f"outside the world: {path}")
149	        rel = p.relative_to(self.root).as_posix() or "."
150	        if rel.split("/", 1)[0] in self.hidden:
151	            raise ValueError(f"not part of the world: {path}")
152	        return p, rel
153	
154	    def _writable(self, rel: str) -> None:
155	        """The goal's tests and the toolchain are the human's; the builder may read them only."""
156	        name = rel.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
157	        for pattern in self.protected:
158	            if pattern.endswith("/"):  # anything under that directory
159	                hit = rel == pattern[:-1] or rel.startswith(pattern)
160	            elif "*" in pattern:  # that basename, anywhere in the world

172	            return f"error: cap reached ({WRITE_CAP} writes and edits); report now"

174	
175	    def list(self, path: str = ".") -> str:
176	        """List one directory of the world: one entry per line as kind, size, path. Path is
177	        relative to the world root; '.' is the root.
178	
179	        Args:
180	            path: The directory to list, relative to the world root.
181	        """
182	        try:
183	            p, rel = self._resolve(path)
184	            if not p.is_dir():
185	                raise ValueError(f"not a directory: {path}")
186	            entries = sorted(p.iterdir(), key=lambda e: (not e.is_dir(), e.name))
187	            if rel == ".":

Edit a file of the world: replace `old` with `new`, once. `old` must appear in the
file exactly once; if it does not, nothing is changed and the count is reported. The
tests and the toolchain cannot be edited.

path.description: The file to edit, relative to the world root.

old.description: The exact text to replace; include lines around it to make it unique.

new.description: The text to put in its place.

function.name: check
function.description:
Run the world's tests and return the exit code and the tail of the output: exit 0 is
green, anything else is red. The tests run in a container, with the world read-only and
no network, so this reports on the world as it is on disk. At most 8 checks per run.

function.name: final_result
function.description: The builder's report: what it changed in the world, and whether the tests pass.

changed.description: The paths you wrote or edited, in order.

did.description: What you changed and why, one fact per item, each naming a path.

check.description: Green or red: the state of the last check.

unsure.description: What you could not determine or verify.

messages.content:
You are the builder. You are given a goal and a world: a directory with code and tests. You
can explore it with `list` and `read`, change it with `write` and `edit`, and test it with
`check`. The goal is reached when `check` is green: the tests are the goal's acceptance
criteria and cannot be changed.

Work in this order: read what the goal touches; run `check` once to see what fails; make the
smallest change that can make it pass; run `check`; repeat. Stop when `check` is green, or
when you cannot make it green within the budget, and return the report through the
`final_result` function: changed (the paths you wrote or edited, in order), did (what you
changed and why, one fact per item, each naming a path), check (green or red), failing (test
names if red), unsure (what you could not determine or verify).

Rules: change only what the goal needs; prefer `edit` over `write` for existing files; never
work around a failing test by changing what it asserts; no commentary outside the report.

1	# factory
2	
3	The factory is `builder.py`: a program that runs a cold model session over a directory, the world, until the world's tests pass, under walls the model cannot cross. It is built one version at a time and its own repository is its first world. Since v0.3 the code is written by `builder.py` itself, from tests written before it runs; the first change it built is commit 48cbbe4. What it can do is read off the records of its runs. Nothing in this repository is written for a model to obey; what holds is held by tests, by the plane and by git.
4	
5	You are the attended agent: a model in some harness, resuming this work cold, working with the owner. This file is for any such model. The state of the work is never narrated here; it is derived from git and the files, as below.
6	
7	## Orient yourself
8	
9	Run these before reading anything else, from the root of the checkout or worktree you are in:
10	
11	```sh
12	uv run python -m unittest -q                                       # the factory's tests; no provider, no network, no docker
13	git tag -l --format='%(refname:strip=2) %(objectname:short)'       # the released versions
14	git log --oneline "tags/$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD"   # what happened since the last one
15	git status --short                                                 # what is not committed; see the last section
16	ls docs/versions docs/seeds                                        # the versions and the backlog
17	ls "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/../runs" | tail -3           # the last run records; see the last section
18	```
19	
20	Then derive:
21	
22	- The version in flight is the note in `docs/versions/` whose name is not a tag. Its seeds are the notes in `docs/seeds/` whose `version` names it.
23	- A seed's stage is its `status`. `open`: evidence and an idea. `spec`: a `## Goal` the builder can be given, assigned to a version. `building`: at least one test names it, `seed: <name>` in the test's docstring, committed red. `done`: merged and green. `docs/templates/seed.md` states what each status requires; `docs/backlog.base` ranks the seeds.
24	- What the builder does and refuses is `README.md`; the walls are the constants at the top of `builder.py`; the exact behaviour is `test_builder.py`.
25	- A run is a directory under `runs/`: read `numbers.json` first (`stopped`, `check`, cost, counts), then `response.md`, `diff.patch` and `wire.jsonl`.
26	
27	## How a version is made
28	
29	The owner and the attended agent choose seeds from the backlog and promote them to specs: a version is assigned, the idea becomes a goal. For each spec the attended agent writes the tests that name the seed, commits them red on a branch in a git worktree, and runs `builder.py` on that worktree with the seed's goal. The factory writes the code. The attended agent reads the record and the diff, commits the diff as the factory's work, merges it, and tags the merge with the version; the version note holds the changelog. The attended agent does not write code the factory could write and does not touch a test to make a build pass, because the factory's ability to do it is what is being measured; the plane refuses the model the same. Tags are plain until seed `the-gate` lands; the gate cuts them annotated with the changelog and renders `CHANGELOG.md`.
30	
31	## Commands
32	
33	- `uv run python -m unittest -v`: the factory's own tests. Nothing external is needed.
34	- `uv run builder.py <world> "<goal>"`: one build. Needs the DeepSeek key in `~/.config/factory/deepseek.key` and docker, since the check runs in a container built once from the world's `uv.lock` and `check.Dockerfile`. Leaves `runs/<utc-stamp>/` beside the `builder.py` that ran, never in the world: run it from the main checkout and pass the worktree as the world. Exits 0 when the model returned a report, 1 on a cap or a provider error, 2 on a usage error. The cost and the time are in the record.
35	- `git worktree add <path> -b <branch>`: a world for a build. `.claude/worktrees/` is an ignored place for one.
36	- `git push origin main --tags`: the mirror is `git@github-joam:yellow-robots/factory.git`. `github-joam` is an SSH alias on this host that selects the owner's key; two GitHub identities share the machine.
37	
38	## Not derivable from the repository
39	
40	- `docs/` is an Obsidian vault the owner keeps open. Obsidian rewrites a file it shows: frontmatter reordered, a `{{...}}` in the frontmatter destroyed, a `.base` file reformatted. A dirty `docs/` may be the owner's content or Obsidian's rewrite; read the diff before committing or discarding it.
41	- A version exists only as a tag. Commit 48cbbe4 is titled `v0.4` and belongs to no version.
42	- Branches `bootstrap` and `v0.1` to `v0.4` are leftovers of past worktrees; `v0.1` to `v0.3` share their names with the tags, so git warns and prefers the tag. Write `tags/v0.3` where it matters.
43	- `runs/` and `plans/` are ignored. The records exist in the main checkout on this host only, until seed `commit-the-runs` lands. `plans/` is scratch for plan files; the plans of v0.2 and v0.3 are appended to their version notes.
44	- The model is DeepSeek `deepseek-flash`. pydantic-ai does not know the name, so `builder.py` carries a profile override; genai-prices has no row for it, so the price table in `builder.py` is the cost source. 1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""The builder: a cold session that changes a world until its tests pass. Factory v0.3.
3	
4	    uv run builder.py <world> "<goal>"
5

7	list, read, write, edit and check. Writes are confined to the world and refused on the goal's
8	tests and the toolchain; check runs the world's tests in a container with no network and the
9	world mounted read-only, so code the model writes never runs on the host and cannot reach the
10	key. The loop is pydantic-ai, pinned; the provider is DeepSeek's chat completions API, the key
11	read from ~/.config/factory/deepseek.key and never written anywhere. Each run leaves
12	runs/<utc-stamp>/ under the factory itself, never in the world, with goal.txt, wire.jsonl (every
13	HTTP attempt as it happened), messages.json (the library's messages), check-<n>.log per check,

66	CHECK_CMD = ("python", "-P", "-m", "unittest", "discover", "-q")

68	CHECK_TAIL_LINES = 60  # lines of check output handed back

71	# Hidden at the root because they are what running, installing and planning the program leave

73	HIDDEN = ("runs", ".claude", "__pycache__", ".venv", "plans", ".git")

75	# what check runs against. A basename glob anywhere, a prefix, or an exact path at the root;
76	# the glob is unittest's own discovery pattern, so every file the check collects is covered.
77	PROTECTED = ("test*.py", "tests/", "pyproject.toml", "uv.lock", "check.Dockerfile", "docs/")

80	
81	ROLE = """\
82	You are the builder. You are given a goal and a world: a directory with code and tests. You
83	can explore it with `list` and `read`, change it with `write` and `edit`, and test it with
84	`check`. The goal is reached when `check` is green: the tests are the goal's acceptance

112	            ("Failing", "failing"), ("Unsure", "unsure"))  # fmt: skip

116	    """The report in v0.1's markdown shape: five headings, one bullet per item."""
117	    out: list[str] = []
118	    for heading, field in SECTIONS:

122	            items = [items]
123	        out.extend(f"- {item}" for item in items or ["(none)"])
124	        out.append("")

128	class Plane:
129	    """The execution plane: what the model can do to the world, and the record of it."""
130	
131	    def __init__(self, root: Path, run_dir: Path, hidden: tuple[str, ...] = HIDDEN,
132	                 protected: tuple[str, ...] = PROTECTED, sandbox: Any = None):  # fmt: skip
133	        self.root = root.resolve()
134	        self.run_dir = run_dir
135	        self.hidden = hidden

145	    def _resolve(self, path: str) -> tuple[Path, str]:
146	        p = (self.root / (path or ".")).resolve()
147	        if p != self.root and self.root not in p.parents:
148	            raise ValueError(f"outside the world: {path}")
149	        rel = p.relative_to(self.root).as_posix() or "."
150	        if rel.split("/", 1)[0] in self.hidden:
151	            raise ValueError(f"not part of the world: {path}")
152	        return p, rel
153	
154	    def _writable(self, rel: str) -> None:
155	        """The goal's tests and the toolchain are the human's; the builder may read them only."""
156	        name = rel.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
157	        for pattern in self.protected:
158	            if pattern.endswith("/"):  # anything under that directory
159	                hit = rel == pattern[:-1] or rel.startswith(pattern)
160	            elif "*" in pattern:  # that basename, anywhere in the world

You are the builder. You are given a goal and a world: a directory with code and tests. You
can explore it with `list` and `read`, change it with `write` and `edit`, and test it with
`check`. The goal is reached when `check` is green: the tests are the goal's acceptance
criteria and cannot be changed.

Work in this order: read what the goal touches; run `check` once to see what fails; make the
smallest change that can make it pass; run `check`; repeat. Stop when `check` is green, or
when you cannot make it green within the budget, and return the report through the
`final_result` function: changed (the paths you wrote or edited, in order), did (what you
changed and why, one fact per item, each naming a path), check (green or red), failing (test
names if red), unsure (what you could not determine or verify).

Rules: change only what the goal needs; prefer `edit` over `write` for existing files; never
work around a failing test by changing what it asserts; no commentary outside the report.

1	# factory
2	
3	The factory is `builder.py`: a program that runs a cold model session over a directory, the world, until the world's tests pass, under walls the model cannot cross. It is built one version at a time and its own repository is its first world. Since v0.3 the code is written by `builder.py` itself, from tests written before it runs; the first change it built is commit 48cbbe4. What it can do is read off the records of its runs. Nothing in this repository is written for a model to obey; what holds is held by tests, by the plane and by git.
4	
5	You are the attended agent: a model in some harness, resuming this work cold, working with the owner. This file is for any such model. The state of the work is never narrated here; it is derived from git and the files, as below.
6	
7	## Orient yourself
8	
9	Run these before reading anything else, from the root of the checkout or worktree you are in:
10	
11	```sh
12	uv run python -m unittest -q                                       # the factory's tests; no provider, no network, no docker
13	git tag -l --format='%(refname:strip=2) %(objectname:short)'       # the released versions
14	git log --oneline "tags/$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD"   # what happened since the last one
15	git status --short                                                 # what is not committed; see the last section
16	ls docs/versions docs/seeds                                        # the versions and the backlog
17	ls "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/../runs" | tail -3           # the last run records; see the last section
18	```
19	
20	Then derive:
21	
22	- The version in flight is the note in `docs/versions/` whose name is not a tag. Its seeds are the notes in `docs/seeds/` whose `version` names it.
23	- A seed's stage is its `status`. `open`: evidence and an idea. `spec`: a `## Goal` the builder can be given, assigned to a version. `building`: at least one test names it, `seed: <name>` in the test's docstring, committed red. `done`: merged and green. `docs/templates/seed.md` states what each status requires; `docs/backlog.base` ranks the seeds.
24	- What the builder does and refuses is `README.md`; the walls are the constants at the top of `builder.py`; the exact behaviour is `test_builder.py`.
25	- A run is a directory under `runs/`: read `numbers.json` first (`stopped`, `check`, cost, counts), then `response.md`, `diff.patch` and `wire.jsonl`.
26	
27	## How a version is made
28	
29	The owner and the attended agent choose seeds from the backlog and promote them to specs: a version is assigned, the idea becomes a goal. For each spec the attended agent writes the tests that name the seed, commits them red on a branch in a git worktree, and runs `builder.py` on that worktree with the seed's goal. The factory writes the code. The attended agent reads the record and the diff, commits the diff as the factory's work, merges it, and tags the merge with the version; the version note holds the changelog. The attended agent does not write code the factory could write and does not touch a test to make a build pass, because the factory's ability to do it is what is being measured; the plane refuses the model the same. Tags are plain until seed `the-gate` lands; the gate cuts them annotated with the changelog and renders `CHANGELOG.md`.
30	
31	## Commands
32	
33	- `uv run python -m unittest -v`: the factory's own tests. Nothing external is needed.
34	- `uv run builder.py <world> "<goal>"`: one build. Needs the DeepSeek key in `~/.config/factory/deepseek.key` and docker, since the check runs in a container built once from the world's `uv.lock` and `check.Dockerfile`. Leaves `runs/<utc-stamp>/` beside the `builder.py` that ran, never in the world: run it from the main checkout and pass the worktree as the world. Exits 0 when the model returned a report, 1 on a cap or a provider error, 2 on a usage error. The cost and the time are in the record.
35	- `git worktree add <path> -b <branch>`: a world for a build. `.claude/worktrees/` is an ignored place for one.
36	- `git push origin main --tags`: the mirror is `git@github-joam:yellow-robots/factory.git`. `github-joam` is an SSH alias on this host that selects the owner's key; two GitHub identities share the machine.
37	
38	## Not derivable from the repository
39

3	The factory is `builder.py`: a program that runs a cold model session over a directory, the world, until the world's tests pass, under walls the model cannot cross. It is built one version at a time and its own repository is its first world. Since v0.3 the code is written by `builder.py` itself, from tests written before it runs; the first change it built is commit 48cbbe4. What it can do is read off the records of its runs. Nothing in this repository is written for a model to obey; what holds is held by tests, by the plane and by git.
4	
5	You are the attended agent: a model in some harness, resuming this work cold, working with the owner. This file is for any such model. The state of the work is never narrated here; it is derived from git and the files, as below.
6	
7	## Orient yourself
8	
9	Run these before reading anything else, from the root of the checkout or worktree you are in:
10	
11	```sh
12	uv run python -m unittest -q                                       # the factory's tests; no provider, no network, no docker
13	git tag -l --format='%(refname:strip=2) %(objectname:short)'       # the released versions
14	git log --oneline "tags/$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD"   # what happened since the last one
15	git status --short                                                 # what is not committed; see the last section
16	ls docs/versions docs/seeds                                        # the versions and the backlog
17	ls "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/../runs" | tail -3           # the last run records; see the last section
18	```
19	
20	Then derive:
21	
22	- The version in flight is the note in `docs/versions/` whose name is not a tag. Its seeds are the notes in `docs/seeds/` whose `version` names it.
23	- A seed's stage is its `status`. `open`: evidence and an idea. `spec`: a `## Goal` the builder can be given, assigned to a version. `building`: at least one test names it, `seed: <name>` in the test's docstring, committed red. `done`: merged and green. `docs/templates/seed.md` states what each status requires; `docs/backlog.base` ranks the seeds.
24	- What the builder does and refuses is `README.md`; the walls are the constants at the top of `builder.py`; the exact behaviour is `test_builder.py`.
25	- A run is a directory under `runs/`: read `numbers.json` first (`stopped`, `check`, cost, counts), then `response.md`, `diff.patch` and `wire.jsonl`.
26	
27	## How a version is made
28	
29	The owner and the attended agent choose seeds from the backlog and promote them to specs: a version is assigned, the idea becomes a goal. For each spec the attended agent writes the tests that name the seed, commits them red on a branch in a git worktree, and runs `builder.py` on that worktree with the seed's goal. The factory writes the code. The attended agent reads the record and the diff, commits the diff as the factory's work, merges it, and tags the merge with the version; the version note holds the changelog. The attended agent does not write code the factory could write and does not touch a test to make a build pass, because the factory's ability to do it is what is being measured; the plane refuses the model the same. Tags are plain until seed `the-gate` lands; the gate cuts them annotated with the changelog and renders `CHANGELOG.md`.

31	## Commands
32	
33	- `uv run python -m unittest -v`: the factory's own tests. Nothing external is needed.
34	- `uv run builder.py <world> "<goal>"`: one build. Needs the DeepSeek key in `~/.config/factory/deepseek.key` and docker, since the check runs in a container built once from the world's `uv.lock` and `check.Dockerfile`. Leaves `runs/<utc-stamp>/` beside the `builder.py` that ran, never in the world: run it from the main checkout and pass the worktree as the world. Exits 0 when the model returned a report, 1 on a cap or a provider error, 2 on a usage error. The cost and the time are in the record.

3	The factory is `builder.py`: a program that runs a cold model session over a directory, the world, until the world's tests pass, under walls the model cannot cross. It is built one version at a time and its own repository is its first world. Since v0.3 the code is written by `builder.py` itself, from tests written before it runs; the first change it built is commit 48cbbe4. What it can do is read off the records of its runs. Nothing in this repository is written for a model to obey; what holds is held by tests, by the plane and by git.
4	
5	You are the attended agent: a model in some harness, resuming this work cold, working with the owner. This file is for any such model. The state of the work is never narrated here; it is derived from git and the files, as below.
6	
7	## Orient yourself
8	
9	Run these before reading anything else, from the root of the checkout or worktree you are in:
10	
11	```sh
12	uv run python -m unittest -q                                       # the factory's tests; no provider, no network, no docker
13	git tag -l --format='%(refname:strip=2) %(objectname:short)'       # the released versions
14	git log --oneline "tags/$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD"   # what happened since the last one
15	git status --short                                                 # what is not committed; see the last section
16	ls docs/versions docs/seeds                                        # the versions and the backlog
17	ls "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/../runs" | tail -3           # the last run records; see the last section
18	```
19	
20	Then derive:
21	
22	- The version in flight is the note in `docs/versions/` whose name is not a tag. Its seeds are the notes in `docs/seeds/` whose `version` names it.
23	- A seed's stage is its `status`. `open`: evidence and an idea. `spec`: a `## Goal` the builder can be given, assigned to a version. `building`: at least one test names it, `seed: <name>` in the test's docstring, committed red. `done`: merged and green. `docs/templates/seed.md` states what each status requires; `docs/backlog.base` ranks the seeds.
24	- What the builder does and refuses is `README.md`; the walls are the constants at the top of `builder.py`; the exact behaviour is `test_builder.py`.
25	- A run is a directory under `runs/`: read `numbers.json` first (`stopped`, `check`, cost, counts), then `response.md`, `diff.patch` and `wire.jsonl`.
26	
27	## How a version is made
28	
29	The owner and the attended agent choose seeds from the backlog and promote them to specs: a version is assigned, the idea becomes a goal. For each spec the attended agent writes the tests that name the seed, commits them red on a branch in a git worktree, and runs `builder.py` on that worktree with the seed's goal. The factory writes the code. The attended agent reads the record and the diff, commits the diff as the factory's work, merges it, and tags the merge with the version; the version note holds the changelog. The attended agent does not write code the factory could write and does not touch a test to make a build pass, because the factory's ability to do it is what is being measured; the plane refuses the model the same. Tags are plain until seed `the-gate` lands; the gate cuts them annotated with the changelog and renders `CHANGELOG.md`.
30	
31	## Commands
32	
33	- `uv run python -m unittest -v`: the factory's own tests. Nothing external is needed.
34	- `uv run builder.py <world> "<goal>"`: one build. Needs the DeepSeek key in `~/.config/factory/deepseek.key` and docker, since the check runs in a container built once from the world's `uv.lock` and `check.Dockerfile`. Leaves `runs/<utc-stamp>/` beside the `builder.py` that ran, never in the world: run it from the main checkout and pass the worktree as the world. Exits 0 when the model returned a report, 1 on a cap or a provider error, 2 on a usage error. The cost and the time are in the record.
35	- `git worktree add <path> -b <branch>`: a world for a build. `.claude/worktrees/` is an ignored place for one.
36	- `git push origin main --tags`: the mirror is `git@github-joam:yellow-robots/factory.git`. `github-joam` is an SSH alias on this host that selects the owner's key; two GitHub identities share the machine.
37	
38	## Not derivable from the repository
39	
40	- `docs/` is an Obsidian vault the owner keeps open. Obsidian rewrites a file it shows: frontmatter reordered, a `{{...}}` in the frontmatter destroyed, a `.base` file reformatted. A dirty `docs/` may be the owner's content or Obsidian's rewrite; read the diff before committing or discarding it.
41	- A version exists only as a tag. Commit 48cbbe4 is titled `v0.4` and belongs to no version.
42	- Branches `bootstrap` and `v0.1` to `v0.4` are leftovers of past worktrees; `v0.1` to `v0.3` share their names with the tags, so git warns and prefers the tag. Write `tags/v0.3` where it matters.
43	- `runs/` and `plans/` are ignored. The records exist in the main checkout on this host only, until seed `commit-the-runs` lands. `plans/` is scratch for plan files; the plans of v0.2 and v0.3 are appended to their version notes.
44	- The model is DeepSeek `deepseek-flash`. pydantic-ai does not know the name, so `builder.py` carries a profile override; genai-prices has no row for it, so the price table in `builder.py` is the cost source. Thinking is on by default and ignores temperature. The key is never printed or committed.
45	- The history before this repository, v1 and the design that was abandoned for it, is in the owner's Obsidian vault at `/srv/obsidian/vaults/obsidian/03 archive/factory-v1/`. Reference, never a plan.

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""The builder: a cold session that changes a world until its tests pass. Factory v0.3.
3	
4	    uv run builder.py <world> "<goal>"
5	
6	The world is the directory named on the command line, reachable only through five functions:
7	list, read, write, edit and check. Writes are confined to the world and refused on the goal's
8	tests and the toolchain; check runs the world's tests in a container with no network and the
9	world mounted read-only, so code the model writes never runs on the host and cannot reach the
10	key. The loop is pydantic-ai, pinned; the provider is DeepSeek's chat completions API, the key
11	read from ~/.config/factory/deepseek.key and never written anywhere. Each run leaves
12	runs/<utc-stamp>/ under the factory itself, never in the world, with goal.txt, wire.jsonl (every
13	HTTP attempt as it happened), messages.json (the library's messages), check-<n>.log per check,

116	    """The report in v0.1's markdown shape: five headings, one bullet per item."""
117	    out: list[str] = []
118	    for heading, field in SECTIONS:

121	        if isinstance(items, str):  # check is one value, and renders as one bullet
122	            items = [items]
123	        out.extend(f"- {item}" for item in items or ["(none)"])
124	        out.append("")
125	    return "\n".join(out)
126	
127	
128	class Plane:
129	    """The execution plane: what the model can do to the world, and the record of it."""
130	
131	    def __init__(self, root: Path, run_dir: Path, hidden: tuple[str, ...] = HIDDEN,
132	                 protected: tuple[str, ...] = PROTECTED, sandbox: Any = None):  # fmt: skip
133	        self.root = root.resolve()
134	        self.run_dir = run_dir
135	        self.hidden = hidden
136	        self.protected = protected
137	        self.sandbox = sandbox
138	        self.listed: list[str] = []
139	        self.read_paths: list[str] = []
140	        self.lines_read = 0
141	        self.written: list[str] = []
142	        self.edited: list[str] = []
143	        self.checks: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
144	
145	    def _resolve(self, path: str) -> tuple[Path, str]:
146	        p = (self.root / (path or ".")).resolve()
147	        if p != self.root and self.root not in p.parents:
148	            raise ValueError(f"outside the world: {path}")
149	        rel = p.relative_to(self.root).as_posix() or "."
150	        if rel.split("/", 1)[0] in self.hidden:
151	            raise ValueError(f"not part of the world: {path}")
152	        return p, rel
153	
154	    def _writable(self, rel: str) -> None:
155	        """The goal's tests and the toolchain are the human's; the builder may read them only."""
156	        name = rel.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
157	        for pattern in self.protected:
158	            if pattern.endswith("/"):  # anything under that directory
159	                hit = rel == pattern[:-1] or rel.startswith(pattern)
160	            elif "*" in pattern:  # that basename, anywhere in the world
161	                hit = fnmatch.fnmatchcase(name, pattern)
162	            else:  # that exact path at the root, not the basename anywhere
163	                hit = rel == pattern

165	                raise ValueError(

167	                    "builder's to change)"
168	                )
169	
170	    def _capped(self) -> str:
171	        if len(self.written) + len(self.edited) >= WRITE_CAP:
172	            return f"error: cap reached ({WRITE_CAP} writes and edits); report now"
173	        return ""
174	
175	    def list(self, path: str = ".") -> str:
176	        """List one directory of the world: one entry per line as kind, size, path. Path is
177	        relative to the world root; '.' is the root.
178	
179	        Args:
180	            path: The directory to list, relative to the world root.
181	        """
182	        try:
183	            p, rel = self._resolve(path)
184	            if not p.is_dir():
185	                raise ValueError(f"not a directory: {path}")
186	            entries = sorted(p.iterdir(), key=lambda e: (not e.is_dir(), e.name))

194	            if len(entries) > LIST_CAP:

197	            return f"error: {e}"

201	    def read(self, path: str, start: int = 1) -> str:
202	        """Read a file of the world as numbered lines, from line `start` (1-based), at most 300
203	        lines or 32000 bytes per call; a truncated read says where to continue.
204	
205	        Args:
206	            path: The file to read, relative to the world root.
207	            start: The first line to read, 1-based.

213	            start = max(1, int(start))

def _highest_tag(tags):
    best = None
    best_key = None
    for tag in tags:
        m = re.match(r"^v(\d+)\.(\d+)$", tag)
        if not m:
            continue
        key = (int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2)))
        if best_key is None or key > best_key:
            best, best_key = tag, key
    return best
