3	The factory is `builder.py`: a program that runs a cold model session over a directory, the world, until the world's tests pass, under walls the model cannot cross. It is built one version at a time and its own repository is its first world. Since v0.3 the code is written by `builder.py` itself, from tests written before it runs; the first change it built is commit 48cbbe4. What it can do is read off the records of its runs. Nothing in this repository is written for a model to obey; what holds is held by tests, by the plane and by git.
4	
5	You are the attended agent: a model in some harness, resuming this work cold, working with the owner. This file is for any such model. The state of the work is never narrated here; it is derived from git and the files, as below.
6	
7	## Orient yourself
8	
9	Run these before reading anything else, from the root of the checkout or worktree you are in:
10	
11	```sh
12	uv run python -m unittest -q                                       # the factory's tests; no provider, no network, no docker
13	git tag -l --format='%(refname:strip=2) %(objectname:short)'       # the released versions
14	git log --oneline "tags/$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD"   # what happened since the last one
15	git status --short                                                 # what is not committed; see the last section
16	ls docs/versions docs/seeds                                        # the versions and the backlog
17	ls "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/../runs" | tail -3           # the last run records; see the last section
18	```
19	
20	Then derive:
21	
22	- The version in flight is the note in `docs/versions/` whose name is not a tag. Its seeds are the notes in `docs/seeds/` whose `version` names it.
23	- A seed's stage is its `status`. `open`: evidence and an idea. `spec`: a `## Goal` the builder can be given, assigned to a version. `building`: at least one test names it, `seed: <name>` in the test's docstring, committed red. `done`: merged and green. `docs/templates/seed.md` states what each status requires; `docs/backlog.base` ranks the seeds.
24	- What the builder does and refuses is `README.md`; the walls are the constants at the top of `builder.py`; the exact behaviour is `test_builder.py`.
25	- A run is a directory under `runs/`: read `numbers.json` first (`stopped`, `check`, cost, counts), then `response.md`, `diff.patch` and `wire.jsonl`.
26	
27	## How a version is made
28	
29	The owner and the attended agent choose seeds from the backlog and promote them to specs: a version is assigned, the idea becomes a goal. For each spec the attended agent writes the tests that name the seed, commits them red on a branch in a git worktree, and runs `builder.py` on that worktree with the seed's goal. The factory writes the code. The attended agent reads the record and the diff, commits the diff as the factory's work, merges it, and tags the merge with the version; the version note holds the changelog. The attended agent does not write code the factory could write and does not touch a test to make a build pass, because the factory's ability to do it is what is being measured; the plane refuses the model the same. Tags are plain until seed `the-gate` lands; the gate cuts them annotated with the changelog and renders `CHANGELOG.md`.
30	
31	## Commands
32	
33	- `uv run python -m unittest -v`: the factory's own tests. Nothing external is needed.
34	- `uv run builder.py <world> "<goal>"`: one build. Needs the DeepSeek key in `~/.config/factory/deepseek.key` and docker, since the check runs in a container built once from the world's `uv.lock` and `check.Dockerfile`. Leaves `runs/<utc-stamp>/` beside the `builder.py` that ran, never in the world: run it from the main checkout and pass the worktree as the world. Exits 0 when the model returned a report, 1 on a cap or a provider error, 2 on a usage error. The cost and the time are in the record.
35	- `git worktree add <path> -b <branch>`: a world for a build. `.claude/worktrees/` is an ignored place for one.
36	- `git push origin main --tags`: the mirror is `git@github-joam:yellow-robots/factory.git`. `github-joam` is an SSH alias on this host that selects the owner's key; two GitHub identities share the machine.

40	- `docs/` is an Obsidian vault the owner keeps open. Obsidian rewrites a file it shows: frontmatter reordered, a `{{...}}` in the frontmatter destroyed, a `.base` file reformatted. A dirty `docs/` may be the owner's content or Obsidian's rewrite; read the diff before committing or discarding it.

43	- `runs/` and `plans/` are ignored. The records exist in the main checkout on this host only, until seed `commit-the-runs` lands. `plans/` is scratch for plan files; the plans of v0.2 and v0.3 are appended to their version notes.

Three commands. Each prints one line per problem on stdout, starting with the path relative to `root` and saying what is missing, and exits 1 if there is any; with nothing to report it prints nothing and exits 0. 1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""The builder: a cold session that changes a world until its tests pass. Factory v0.3.
3	
4	    uv run builder.py <world> "<goal>"
5	
6	The world is the directory named on the command line, reachable only through five functions:
7	list, read, write, edit and check. Writes are confined to the world and refused on the goal's
8	tests and the toolchain; check runs the world's tests in a container with no network and the
9	world mounted read-only, so code the model writes never runs on the host and cannot reach the
10	key. The loop is pydantic-ai, pinned; the provider is DeepSeek's chat completions API, the key
11	read from ~/.config/factory/deepseek.key and never written anywhere. Each run leaves
12	runs/<utc-stamp>/ under the factory itself, never in the world, with goal.txt, wire.jsonl (every
13	HTTP attempt as it happened), messages.json (the library's messages), check-<n>.log per check,
14	diff.patch (what the run left in the world), report.json, response.md (the report rendered) and
15	numbers.json.
16	"""
17

52	RUNS = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "runs"  # the factory's record, never inside the world
53	KEY_FILE = Path.home() / ".config" / "factory" / "deepseek.key"
54	MODEL = "deepseek-flash"
55	LIBRARY = "pydantic-ai-slim " + importlib.metadata.version("pydantic-ai-slim")
56	TOOL_CALLS_CAP = 80  # tool calls per run; over it the run stops with no report
57	REQUEST_CAP = 60  # provider requests per run
58	LIST_CAP = 500  # entries per list
59	READ_LINES_CAP = 300  # lines per read
60	READ_BYTES_CAP = 32_000  # bytes per read
61	WRITE_CAP = 30  # writes and edits per run, together
62	CHECK_CAP = 8  # checks per run
63	# What green means, in the world's own terms. -P keeps the world's root off sys.path while the
64	# runner is imported, or a file named unittest.py at the world root shadows the stdlib and turns
65	# any suite green; `discover` still finds the world's tests and puts the root back for them.
66	CHECK_CMD = ("python", "-P", "-m", "unittest", "discover", "-q")
67	CHECK_TIMEOUT = 120  # seconds for one check, then the container is killed
68	CHECK_TAIL_LINES = 60  # lines of check output handed back
69	CHECK_TAIL_BYTES = 8_000  # and at most this many bytes of them
70	IMAGE_TIMEOUT = 600  # seconds for the one image build
71	# Hidden at the root because they are what running, installing and planning the program leave
72	# behind, not the world; .git is the human's record and its hooks run on the host.
73	HIDDEN = ("runs", ".claude", "__pycache__", ".venv", "plans", ".git")
74	# Refused to write and edit: the tests are the goal's acceptance criteria and the toolchain is
75	# what check runs against. A basename glob anywhere, a prefix, or an exact path at the root;
76	# the glob is unittest's own discovery pattern, so every file the check collects is covered.
77	PROTECTED = ("test*.py", "tests/", "pyproject.toml", "uv.lock", "check.Dockerfile", "docs/")
78	# USD per 1M tokens, peak rates; api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing read on 2026-09-15.
79	PRICE = {"cache_hit": 0.006, "cache_miss": 0.3, "output": 1.2}
80	
81	ROLE = """\
82	You are the builder. You are given a goal and a world: a directory with code and tests. You
83	can explore it with `list` and `read`, change it with `write` and `edit`, and test it with
84	`check`. The goal is reached when `check` is green: the tests are the goal's acceptance
85	criteria and cannot be changed.
86	
87	Work in this order: read what the goal touches; run `check` once to see what fails; make the
88	smallest change that can make it pass; run `check`; repeat. Stop when `check` is green, or
89	when you cannot make it green within the budget, and return the report through the
90	`final_result` function: changed (the paths you wrote or edited, in order), did (what you
91	changed and why, one fact per item, each naming a path), check (green or red), failing (test
92	names if red), unsure (what you could not determine or verify).
93	
94	Rules: change only what the goal needs; prefer `edit` over `write` for existing files; never
95	work around a failing test by changing what it asserts; no commentary outside the report.
96	"""
97	
98	
99	class BuildReport(BaseModel):
100	    """The builder's report: what it changed in the world, and whether the tests pass."""
101	
102	    changed: list[str] = Field(description="The paths you wrote or edited, in order.")
103	    did: list[str] = Field(
104	        description="What you changed and why, one fact per item, each naming a path."
105	    )
106	    check: Literal["green", "red"] = Field(description="Green or red: the state of the last check.")
107	    failing: list[str] = Field(description="Test names if red.")
108	    unsure: list[str] = Field(description="What you could not determine or verify.")
109	
110	
111	SECTIONS = (("Changed", "changed"), ("Did", "did"), ("Check", "check"),
112	            ("Failing", "failing"), ("Unsure", "unsure"))  # fmt: skip
113	
114	
115	def render(report: BuildReport) -> str:
116	    """The report in v0.1's markdown shape: five headings, one bullet per item."""
117	    out: list[str] = []
118	    for heading, field in SECTIONS:
119	        out.append(f"## {heading}")
120	        items = getattr(report, field)
121	        if isinstance(items, str):  # check is one value, and renders as one bullet
122	            items = [items]
123	        out.extend(f"- {item}" for item in items or ["(none)"])
124	        out.append("")
125	    return "\n".join(out)
126	
127	
128	class Plane:
129	    """The execution plane: what the model can do to the world, and the record of it."""
130	
131	    def __init__(self, root: Path, run_dir: Path, hidden: tuple[str, ...] = HIDDEN,
132	                 protected: tuple[str, ...] = PROTECTED, sandbox: Any = None):  # fmt: skip
133	        self.root = root.resolve()
134	        self.run_dir = run_dir
135	        self.hidden = hidden
136	        self.protected = protected
137	        self.sandbox = sandbox
138	        self.listed: list[str] = []
139	        self.read_paths: list[str] = []
140	        self.lines_read = 0
141	        self.written: list[str] = []
142	        self.edited: list[str] = []
143	        self.checks: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
144	
145	    def _resolve(self, path: str) -> tuple[Path, str]:
146	        p = (self.root / (path or ".")).resolve()
147	        if p != self.root and self.root not in p.parents:
148	            raise ValueError(f"outside the world: {path}")
149	        rel = p.relative_to(self.root).as_posix() or "."
150	        if rel.split("/", 1)[0] in self.hidden:
151	            raise ValueError(f"not part of the world: {path}")
152	        return p, rel
153	
154	    def _writable(self, rel: str) -> None:
155	        """The goal's tests and the toolchain are the human's; the builder may read them only."""
156	        name = rel.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
157	        for pattern in self.protected:
158	            if pattern.endswith("/"):  # anything under that directory
159	                hit = rel == pattern[:-1] or rel.startswith(pattern)
160	            elif "*" in pattern:  # that basename, anywhere in the world
161	                hit = fnmatch.fnmatchcase(name, pattern)
162	            else:  # that exact path at the root, not the basename anywhere
163	                hit = rel == pattern
164	            if hit:
165	                raise ValueError(
166	                    f"protected: {rel} (the goal's tests and the toolchain are not the "
167	                    "builder's to change)"
168	                )
169	
170	    def _capped(self) -> str:
171	        if len(self.written) + len(self.edited) >= WRITE_CAP:
172	            return f"error: cap reached ({WRITE_CAP} writes and edits); report now"
173	        return ""
174	
175	    def list(self, path: str = ".") -> str:
176	        """List one directory of the world: one entry per line as kind, size, path. Path is
177	        relative to the world root; '.' is the root.
178	
179	        Args:
180	            path: The directory to list, relative to the world root.
181	        """
182	        try:
183	            p, rel = self._resolve(path)
184	            if not p.is_dir():
185	                raise ValueError(f"not a directory: {path}")
186	            entries = sorted(p.iterdir(), key=lambda e: (not e.is_dir(), e.name))
187	            if rel == ".":
188	                entries = [e for e in entries if e.name not in self.hidden]
189	            lines = []

191	                kind = "link" if e.is_symlink() else "dir" if e.is_dir() else "file"
192	                size = e.lstat().st_size if kind == "file" else 0
193	                lines.append(f"{kind}\t{size}\t{e.relative_to(self.root).as_posix()}")
194	            if len(entries) > LIST_CAP:
195	                lines.append(f"...\t{len(entries) - LIST_CAP} more entries not shown")
196	        except (ValueError, OSError, RuntimeError) as e:  # RuntimeError: a symlink loop
197	            return f"error: {e}"
198	        self.listed.append(rel)
199	        return "\n".join(lines) or "(empty)"
200	
201	    def read(self, path: str, start: int = 1) -> str:
202	        """Read a file of the world as numbered lines, from line `start` (1-based), at most 300
203	        lines or 32000 bytes per call; a truncated read says where to continue.
204	
205	        Args:
206	            path: The file to read, relative to the world root.
207	            start: The first line to read, 1-based.
208	        """
209	        try:
210	            p, rel = self._resolve(path)
211	            if not p.is_file():
212	                raise ValueError(f"not a file: {path}")
213	            start = max(1, int(start))
214	            out: list[str] = []
215	            n = nbytes = 0
216	            with p.open("r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
217	                for i, line in enumerate(f, 1):
218	                    if i < start:
219	                        continue
220	                    size = len(line.encode())
221	                    if n >= READ_LINES_CAP or nbytes + size > READ_BYTES_CAP:
222	                        if n:  # one line per call at least, or a long line dead-ends the read
223	                            out.append(f"...\ttruncated; continue with start={i}")
224	                            break
225	                        cut = line.encode()[:READ_BYTES_CAP].decode("utf-8", "ignore")
226	                        out.append(f"{i}\t{cut} …(line cut at {READ_BYTES_CAP} bytes)")
227	                    else:
228	                        out.append(f"{i}\t{line.rstrip(chr(10))}")
229	                    n += 1
230	                    nbytes += size
231	        except (ValueError, OSError, RuntimeError) as e:  # RuntimeError: a symlink loop
232	            return f"error: {e}"
233	        self.read_paths.append(rel)
234	        self.lines_read += n
235	        return "\n".join(out) or "(empty)"
236	
237	    def write(self, path: str, content: str) -> str:
238	        """Write a file of the world: create it, or replace what is there with `content`.
239	        Directories on the way are created. The tests and the toolchain cannot be written.
240	
241	        Args:
242	            path: The file to write, relative to the world root.
243	            content: The whole text of the file, as it should be afterwards.
244	        """
245	        capped = self._capped()
246	        if capped:

248	        try:

2	
3	The factory is `builder.py`: a program that runs a cold model session over a directory, the world, until the world's tests pass, under walls the model cannot cross. It is built one version at a time and its own repository is its first world. Since v0.3 the code is written by `builder.py` itself, from tests written before it runs; the first change it built is commit 48cbbe4. What it can do is read off the records of its runs. Nothing in this repository is written for a model to obey; what holds is held by tests, by the plane and by git.
4	
5	You are the attended agent: a model in some harness, resuming this work cold, working with the owner. This file is for any such model. The state of the work is never narrated here; it is derived from git and the files, as below.
6	
7	## Orient yourself
8	
9	Run these before reading anything else, from the root of the checkout or worktree you are in:
10	
11	```sh
12	uv run python -m unittest -q                                       # the factory's tests; no provider, no network, no docker
13	git tag -l --format='%(refname:strip=2) %(objectname:short)'       # the released versions
14	git log --oneline "tags/$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD"   # what happened since the last one
15	git status --short                                                 # what is not committed; see the last section
16	ls docs/versions docs/seeds                                        # the versions and the backlog
17	ls "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/../runs" | tail -3           # the last run records; see the last section
18	```
19	
20	Then derive:
21	
22	- The version in flight is the note in `docs/versions/` whose name is not a tag. Its seeds are the notes in `docs/seeds/` whose `version` names it.
23	- A seed's stage is its `status`. `open`: evidence and an idea. `spec`: a `## Goal` the builder can be given, assigned to a version. `building`: at least one test names it, `seed: <name>` in the test's docstring, committed red. `done`: merged and green. `docs/templates/seed.md` states what each status requires; `docs/backlog.base` ranks the seeds.
24	- What the builder does and refuses is `README.md`; the walls are the constants at the top of `builder.py`; the exact behaviour is `test_builder.py`.
25	- A run is a directory under `runs/`: read `numbers.json` first (`stopped`, `check`, cost, counts), then `response.md`, `diff.patch` and `wire.jsonl`.
26	
27	## How a version is made
28	
29	The owner and the attended agent choose seeds from the backlog and promote them to specs: a version is assigned, the idea becomes a goal. For each spec the attended agent writes the tests that name the seed, commits them red on a branch in a git worktree, and runs `builder.py` on that worktree with the seed's goal. The factory writes the code. The attended agent reads the record and the diff, commits the diff as the factory's work, merges it, and tags the merge with the version; the version note holds the changelog. The attended agent does not write code the factory could write and does not touch a test to make a build pass, because the factory's ability to do it is what is being measured; the plane refuses the model the same. Tags are plain until seed `the-gate` lands; the gate cuts them annotated with the changelog and renders `CHANGELOG.md`.
30	
31	## Commands
32	
33	- `uv run python -m unittest -v`: the factory's own tests. Nothing external is needed.
34	- `uv run builder.py <world> "<goal>"`: one build. Needs the DeepSeek key in `~/.config/factory/deepseek.key` and docker, since the check runs in a container built once from the world's `uv.lock` and `check.Dockerfile`. Leaves `runs/<utc-stamp>/` beside the `builder.py` that ran, never in the world: run it from the main checkout and pass the worktree as the world. Exits 0 when the model returned a report, 1 on a cap or a provider error, 2 on a usage error. The cost and the time are in the record.
35	- `git worktree add <path> -b <branch>`: a world for a build. `.claude/worktrees/` is an ignored place for one.

    if command == "render":

    if command == "release":

            return usage()
        problems = release(root, args[2])
        return report(problems)
    return usage()
```

def _highest_tag(tags):
    best = None
    best_key = None
    for tag in tags:
        m = re.match(r"^v(\d+)\.(\d+)$", tag)
        if not m:
            continue
        key = (int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2)))
        if best_key is None or key > best_key:
            best, best_key = tag, key
    return best

def _first_paragraph(body):
    lines = body.splitlines()
    started = False
    para = []
    for line in lines:
        s = line.strip()
        if not started:
            if s.startswith("# "):
                started = True
            continue
        if not s:
            if para:
                break
            continue
        if s.startswith("#") or s.startswith("![[") or s.startswith("- "):
            if para:
                break
            continue
        para.append(s)
    return " ".join(para)

3	The factory is `builder.py`: a program that runs a cold model session over a directory, the world, until the world's tests pass, under walls the model cannot cross. It is built one version at a time and its own repository is its first world. Since v0.3 the code is written by `builder.py` itself, from tests written before it runs; the first change it built is commit 48cbbe4. What it can do is read off the records of its runs. Nothing in this repository is written for a model to obey; what holds is held by tests, by the plane and by git.
4	
5	You are the attended agent: a model in some harness, resuming this work cold, working with the owner. This file is for any such model. The state of the work is never narrated here; it is derived from git and the files, as below.
6	
7	## Orient yourself
8	
9	Run these before reading anything else, from the root of the checkout or worktree you are in:
10	
11	```sh
12	uv run python -m unittest -q                                       # the factory's tests; no provider, no network, no docker
13	git tag -l --format='%(refname:strip=2) %(objectname:short)'       # the released versions
14	git log --oneline "tags/$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD"   # what happened since the last one
15	git status --short                                                 # what is not committed; see the last section

17	ls "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/../runs" | tail -3           # the last run records; see the last section

20	Then derive:
21	
22	- The version in flight is the note in `docs/versions/` whose name is not a tag. Its seeds are the notes in `docs/seeds/` whose `version` names it.
23	- A seed's stage is its `status`. `open`: evidence and an idea. `spec`: a `## Goal` the builder can be given, assigned to a version. `building`: at least one test names it, `seed: <name>` in the test's docstring, committed red. `done`: merged and green. `docs/templates/seed.md` states what each status requires; `docs/backlog.base` ranks the seeds.
24	- What the builder does and refuses is `README.md`; the walls are the constants at the top of `builder.py`; the exact behaviour is `test_builder.py`.
25	- A run is a directory under `runs/`: read `numbers.json` first (`stopped`, `check`, cost, counts), then `response.md`, `diff.patch` and `wire.jsonl`.
26	
27	## How a version is made
28	
29	The owner and the attended agent choose seeds from the backlog and promote them to specs: a version is assigned, the idea becomes a goal. For each spec the attended agent writes the tests that name the seed, commits them red on a branch in a git worktree, and runs `builder.py` on that worktree with the seed's goal. The factory writes the code. The attended agent reads the record and the diff, commits the diff as the factory's work, merges it, and tags the merge with the version; the version note holds the changelog. The attended agent does not write code the factory could write and does not touch a test to make a build pass, because the factory's ability to do it is what is being measured; the plane refuses the model the same. 33	- `uv run python -m unittest -v`: the factory's own tests. Nothing external is needed.

2	"""The builder: a cold session that changes a world until its tests pass. Factory v0.3.
3	
4	    uv run builder.py <world> "<goal>"
5	
6	The world is the directory named on the command line, reachable only through five functions:
7	list, read, write, edit and check. Writes are confined to the world and refused on the goal's
8	tests and the toolchain; check runs the world's tests in a container with no network and the
9	world mounted read-only, so code the model writes never runs on the host and cannot reach the
10	key. The loop is pydantic-ai, pinned; the provider is DeepSeek's chat completions API, the key
11	read from ~/.config/factory/deepseek.key and never written anywhere. Each run leaves
12	runs/<utc-stamp>/ under the factory itself, never in the world, with goal.txt, wire.jsonl (every
13	HTTP attempt as it happened), messages.json (the library's messages), check-<n>.log per check,

81	ROLE = """\
82	You are the builder. You are given a goal and a world: a directory with code and tests. You
83	can explore it with `list` and `read`, change it with `write` and `edit`, and test it with

99	class BuildReport(BaseModel):

115	def render(report: BuildReport) -> str:
116	    """The report in v0.1's markdown shape: five headings, one bullet per item."""

131	    def __init__(self, root: Path, run_dir: Path, hidden: tuple[str, ...] = HIDDEN,

145	    def _resolve(self, path: str) -> tuple[Path, str]:

174	
175	    def list(self, path: str = ".") -> str:
176	        """List one directory of the world: one entry per line as kind, size, path. Path is

203	        lines or 32000 bytes per call; a truncated read says where to continue.

2	"""The builder: a cold session that changes a world until its tests pass. Factory v0.3.

370	    if not bullets:

390	    body = frontmatter(_read(note))[1]
391	    paragraph = _first_paragraph(body)
392	    bullets = _changelog_bullets(body)
393	    message = paragraph
394	    if bullets:

398	        cwd=str(root),

415	def main(argv: list[str], root: Path | str | None = None) -> int:
416	    root = Path(root) if root is not None else Path(__file__).resolve().parent
417	    args = list(argv)
418	    if len(args) < 2 or not args[1].strip():
419	        return _usage()

425	    if command == "release":

21	
22	- The version in flight is the note in `docs/versions/` whose name is not a tag. Its seeds are the notes in `docs/seeds/` whose `version` names it.
23	- A seed's stage is its `status`. `open`: evidence and an idea. `spec`: a `## Goal` the builder can be given, assigned to a version. `building`: at least one test names it, `seed: <name>` in the test's docstring, committed red. `done`: merged and green. `docs/templates/seed.md` states what each status requires; `docs/backlog.base` ranks the seeds.

28	
29	The owner and the attended agent choose seeds from the backlog and promote them to specs: a version is assigned, the idea becomes a goal. For each spec the attended agent writes the tests that name the seed, commits them red on a branch in a git worktree, and runs `builder.py` on that worktree with the seed's goal. The factory writes the code. The attended agent reads the record and the diff, commits the diff as the factory's work, merges it, and tags the merge with the version; the version note holds the changelog. 1	# factory
2	
3	The factory is `builder.py`: a program that runs a cold model session over a directory, the world, until the world's tests pass, under walls the model cannot cross. It is built one version at a time and its own repository is its first world. Since v0.3 the code is written by `builder.py` itself, from tests written before it runs; the first change it built is commit 48cbbe4. What it can do is read off the records of its runs. Nothing in this repository is written for a model to obey; what holds is held by tests, by the plane and by git.
4	
5	You are the attended agent: a model in some harness, resuming this work cold, working with the owner. This file is for any such model. The state of the work is never narrated here; it is derived from git and the files, as below.
6	
7	## Orient yourself
8	
9	Run these before reading anything else, from the root of the checkout or worktree you are in:
10	
11	```sh
12	uv run python -m unittest -q                                       # the factory's tests; no provider, no network, no docker
13	git tag -l --format='%(refname:strip=2) %(objectname:short)'       # the released versions
14	git log --oneline "tags/$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD"   # what happened since the last one
15	git status --short                                                 # what is not committed; see the last section
16	ls docs/versions docs/seeds                                        # the versions and the backlog
17	ls "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/../runs" | tail -3           # the last run records; see the last section
18	```
19	
20	Then derive:
21	
22	- The version in flight is the note in `docs/versions/` whose name is not a tag. Its seeds are the notes in `docs/seeds/` whose `version` names it.
23	- A seed's stage is its `status`. `open`: evidence and an idea. `spec`: a `## Goal` the builder can be given, assigned to a version. `building`: at least one test names it, `seed: <name>` in the test's docstring, committed red. `done`: merged and green. `docs/templates/seed.md` states what each status requires; `docs/backlog.base` ranks the seeds.
24	- What the builder does and refuses is `README.md`; the walls are the constants at the top of `builder.py`; the exact behaviour is `test_builder.py`.
25	- A run is a directory under `runs/`: read `numbers.json` first (`stopped`, `check`, cost, counts), then `response.md`, `diff.patch` and `wire.jsonl`.
26	
27	## How a version is made
28	
29	The owner and the attended agent choose seeds from the backlog and promote them to specs: a version is assigned, the idea becomes a goal. For each spec the attended agent writes the tests that name the seed, commits them red on a branch in a git worktree, and runs `builder.py` on that worktree with the seed's goal. The factory writes the code. The attended agent reads the record and the diff, commits the diff as the factory's work, merges it, and tags the merge with the version; the version note holds the changelog. The attended agent does not write code the factory could write and does not touch a test to make a build pass, because the factory's ability to do it is what is being measured; the plane refuses the model the same. Tags are plain until seed `the-gate` lands; the gate cuts them annotated with the changelog and renders `CHANGELOG.md`.
30	
31	## Commands
32	
33	- `uv run python -m unittest -v`: the factory's own tests. Nothing external is needed.
34	- `uv run builder.py <world> "<goal>"`: one build. Needs the DeepSeek key in `~/.config/factory/deepseek.key` and docker, since the check runs in a container built once from the world's `uv.lock` and `check.Dockerfile`. Leaves `runs/<utc-stamp>/` beside the `builder.py` that ran, never in the world: run it from the main checkout and pass the worktree as the world. Exits 0 when the model returned a report, 1 on a cap or a provider error, 2 on a usage error. The cost and the time are in the record.
35	- `git worktree add <path> -b <branch>`: a world for a build. `.claude/worktrees/` is an ignored place for one.
36	- `git push origin main --tags`: the mirror is `git@github-joam:yellow-robots/factory.git`. `github-joam` is an SSH alias on this host that selects the owner's key; two GitHub identities share the machine.

    best = None
    best_key = None
    for tag in tags:
        m = re.match(r"^v(\d+)\.(\d+)$", tag)
        if not m:
            continue
        key = (int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2)))
        if best_key is None or key > best_key:
            best, best_key = tag, key
    return best

    lines = body.splitlines()

        s = line.strip()
        if not started:

            continue
        if s.startswith("#") or s.startswith("![[") or s.startswith("- "):
            if para:
                break
            continue
        para.append(s)
    return " ".join(para)

1	# factory
2	
3	The factory is `builder.py`: a program that runs a cold model session over a directory, the world, until the world's tests pass, under walls the model cannot cross. It is built one version at a time and its own repository is its first world. Since v0.3 the code is written by `builder.py` itself, from tests written before it runs; the first change it built is commit 48cbbe4. What it can do is read off the records of its runs. Nothing in this repository is written for a model to obey; what holds is held by tests, by the plane and by git.
4	
5	You are the attended agent: a model in some harness, resuming this work cold, working with the owner. This file is for any such model. The state of the work is never narrated here; it is derived from git and the files, as below.
6	
7	## Orient yourself
8	
9	Run these before reading anything else, from the root of the checkout or worktree you are in:
10	
11	```sh
12	uv run python -m unittest -q                                       # the factory's tests; no provider, no network, no docker
13	git tag -l --format='%(refname:strip=2) %(objectname:short)'       # the released versions
14	git log --oneline "tags/$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD"   # what happened since the last one
15	git status --short                                                 # what is not committed; see the last section
16	ls docs/versions docs/seeds                                        # the versions and the backlog
17	ls "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/../runs" | tail -3           # the last run records; see the last section
18	```
19	
20	Then derive:
21	
22	- The version in flight is the note in `docs/versions/` whose name is not a tag. Its seeds are the notes in `docs/seeds/` whose `version` names it.
23	- A seed's stage is its `status`. `open`: evidence and an idea. `spec`: a `## Goal` the builder can be given, assigned to a version. `building`: at least one test names it, `seed: <name>` in the test's docstring, committed red. `done`: merged and green. `docs/templates/seed.md` states what each status requires; `docs/backlog.base` ranks the seeds.
24	- What the builder does and refuses is `README.md`; the walls are the constants at the top of `builder.py`; the exact behaviour is `test_builder.py`.
25	- A run is a directory under `runs/`: read `numbers.json` first (`stopped`, `check`, cost, counts), then `response.md`, `diff.patch` and `wire.jsonl`.
26	
27	## How a version is made
28	
29	The owner and the attended agent choose seeds from the backlog and promote them to specs: a version is assigned, the idea becomes a goal. For each spec the attended agent writes the tests that name the seed, commits them red on a branch in a git worktree, and runs `builder.py` on that worktree with the seed's goal. The factory writes the code. The attended agent reads the record and the diff, commits the diff as the factory's work, merges it, and tags the merge with the version; the version note holds the changelog. The attended agent does not write code the factory could write and does not touch a test to make a build pass, because the factory's ability to do it is what is being measured; the plane refuses the model the same. Tags are plain until seed `the-gate` lands; the gate cuts them annotated with the changelog and renders `CHANGELOG.md`.
30	
31	## Commands
32	
33	- `uv run python -m unittest -v`: the factory's own tests. Nothing external is needed.
34	- `uv run builder.py <world> "<goal>"`: one build. Needs the DeepSeek key in `~/.config/factory/deepseek.key` and docker, since the check runs in a container built once from the world's `uv.lock` and `check.Dockerfile`. Leaves `runs/<utc-stamp>/` beside the `builder.py` that ran, never in the world: run it from the main checkout and pass the worktree as the world. Exits 0 when the model returned a report, 1 on a cap or a provider error, 2 on a usage error. The cost and the time are in the record.
35	- `git worktree add <path> -b <branch>`: a world for a build. `.claude/worktrees/` is an ignored place for one.
36	- `git push origin main --tags`: the mirror is `git@github-joam:yellow-robots/factory.git`. `github-joam` is an SSH alias on this host that selects the owner's key; two GitHub identities share the machine.

28	
29	The owner and the attended agent choose seeds from the backlog and promote them to specs: a version is assigned, the idea becomes a goal. For each spec the attended agent writes the tests that name the seed, commits them red on a branch in a git worktree, and runs `builder.py` on that worktree with the seed's goal. The factory writes the code. The attended agent reads the record and the diff, commits the diff as the factory's work, merges it, and tags the merge with the version; the version note holds the changelog. The attended agent does not write code the factory could write and does not touch a test to make a build pass, because the factory's ability to do it is what is being measured; the plane refuses the model the same. def _highest_tag(tags):
    best = None
    best_key = None
    for tag in tags:
        m = re.match(r"^v(\d+)\.(\d+)$", tag)
        if not m:
            continue
        key = (int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2)))
        if best_key is None or key > best_key:
            best, best_key = tag, key
    return best
```

def _first_paragraph(body):
    lines = body.splitlines()
    started = False
    para = []
    for line in lines:
        s = line.strip()
        if not started:
            if s.startswith("# "):
                started = True
            continue
        if not s:
            if para:
                break
            continue
        if s.startswith("#") or s.startswith("![[") or s.startswith("- "):
            if para:
                break
            continue
        para.append(s)
    return " ".join(para)
```

3	The factory is `builder.py`: a program that runs a cold model session over a directory, the world, until the world's tests pass, under walls the model cannot cross. It is built one version at a time and its own repository is its first world. Nothing in this repository is written for a model to obey; what holds is held by tests, by the plane and by git.
4	
5	You are the attended agent: a model in some harness, resuming this work cold, working with the owner. This file is for any such model. The state of the work is never narrated here; it is derived from git and the files, as below.
6	
7	## Orient yourself
8	
9	Run these before reading anything else, from the root of the checkout or worktree you are in:
10	
11	```sh
12	uv run python -m unittest -q                                       # the factory's tests; no provider, no network, no docker

21	
22	- The version in flight is the note in `docs/versions/` whose name is not a tag. Its seeds are the notes in `docs/seeds/` whose `version` names it.
23	- A seed's stage is its `status`. `open`: evidence and an idea. `spec`: a `## Goal` the builder can be given, assigned to a version. `building`: at least one test names it, `seed: <name>` in the test's docstring, committed red. `done`: merged and green. `docs/templates/seed.md` states what each status requires; `docs/backlog.base` ranks the seeds.

27	## How a version is made
28	
29	The owner and the attended agent choose seeds from the backlog and promote them to specs: a version is assigned, the idea becomes a goal. For each spec the attended agent writes the tests that name the seed, commits them red on a branch in a git worktree, and runs `builder.py` on that worktree with the seed's goal. The factory writes the code. The attended agent reads the record and the diff, commits the diff as the factory's work, merges it, and tags the merge with the version; the version note holds the changelog. The attended agent does not write code the factory could write and does not touch a test to make a build pass, because the factory's ability to do it is what is being measured; the plane refuses the model the same. 34	- `uv run builder.py <world> "<goal>"`: one build. 2	"""The gate: a deterministic check of the vault, its changelog and its tags.
3	
4	    uv run gate.py check
5	    uv run gate.py render
6	    uv run gate.py release <version>
7	
8	`check` validates `docs/` and the repository against it, `render` writes `CHANGELOG.md` from
9	the tags, and `release` refuses until everything derived agrees, then tags and renders. Each
10	command prints one line per problem on stdout, starting with the path relative to the root,
11	and exits 1 if there is any; with nothing to report it prints nothing and exits 0. Usage errors
12	go to stderr and exit 2.
13	"""

18	import re
19	import subprocess

21	from pathlib import Path

23	USAGE = "usage: gate.py check|render|release <version>"
24	STATUSES = ("open", "spec", "building", "done", "rejected")
25	SEED_FIELDS = {"type", "status", "summary", "value", "effort", "version"}
26	EFFORTS = {"S", "M", "L"}
27	VERSION_NAME = re.compile(r"^v(\d+)\.(\d+)\.md$")
28	VERSION = re.compile(r"^v(\d+)\.(\d+)$")
29	WIKILINK = re.compile(r"\[\[([^\[\]]+)\]\]")

32	def _read(path: Path) -> str:
33	    try:
34	        return path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
35	    except OSError:
36	        return ""

39	def frontmatter(text: str) -> tuple[dict[str, str] | None, str]:
40	    """The `key: value` block between the leading `---` lines, and the body after it."""
41	    lines = text.splitlines()
42	    if not lines or lines[0].strip() != "---":
43	        return None, text
44	    for i in range(1, len(lines)):
45	        if lines[i].strip() == "---":
46	            fields: dict[str, str] = {}
47	            for line in lines[1:i]:
48	                key, sep, value = line.partition(":")
49	                if sep:
50	                    fields[key.strip()] = value.strip()
51	            return fields, "\n".join(lines[i + 1:])
52	    return None, text

55	def _notes(docs: Path) -> list[Path]:
56	    """Every `.md` under `docs/`, the templates excepted."""
57	    templates = docs / "templates"
58	    return [p for p in sorted(docs.rglob("*.md")) if templates not in p.parents]

62	    try:
63	        done = subprocess.run(
64	            ["git", *args], cwd=str(root), capture_output=True, text=True
65	        )

75	def _highest_tag(tags: set[str]) -> str | None:
76	    best, best_key = None, None
77	    for tag in tags:
78	        match = VERSION.match(tag)
79	        if not match:
80	            continue
81	        key = (int(match.group(1)), int(match.group(2)))
82	        if best_key is None or key > best_key:
83	            best, best_key = tag, key
84	    return best

87	def _resolve(target: str, docs: Path) -> bool:
88	    """A note in `docs/`, by path or by name, or a `.base` file."""
89	    target = target.strip()
90	    if not target:
91	        return False
92	    direct = docs / target
93	    if direct.is_file():
94	        return True
95	    if direct.suffix == "" and (docs / (target + ".md")).is_file():
96	        return True
97	    name = target.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
98	    stem = name[:-3] if name.endswith(".md") else name
99	    for found in docs.rglob("*"):
100	        if found.is_file() and (found.name == name or found.stem == stem):
101	            return True
102	    return False

105	def _goal_text(body: str) -> bool:
106	    lines = body.splitlines()
107	    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
108	        if line.strip() != "## Goal":
109	            continue
110	        for after in lines[i + 1:]:
111	            if after.strip().startswith("#"):
112	                break
113	            if after.strip():
114	                return True
115	        return False
116	    return False

119	def _test_docstrings(root: Path) -> list[str]:
120	    """The docstrings of every test method or class in a `test*.py` at the root."""
121	    found: list[str] = []
122	    for path in sorted(root.glob("test*.py")):
123	        if not path.is_file():
124	            continue
125	        try:
126	            tree = ast.parse(_read(path))
127	        except SyntaxError:
128	            continue
129	        for node in ast.walk(tree):
130	            if isinstance(node, ast.ClassDef) or (
131	                isinstance(node, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef))
132	                and node.name.startswith("test")
133	            ):
134	                doc = ast.get_docstring(node)
135	                if doc:
136	                    found.append(doc)
137	    return found

140	def _named_by_a_test(root: Path, stem: str, docstrings: list[str]) -> bool:
141	    pattern = re.compile(rf"seed:\s*{re.escape(stem)}(?![\w-])")
142	    return any(pattern.search(doc) for doc in docstrings)

145	def problems_check(root: Path) -> list[str]:
146	    root = Path(root)
147	    docs = root / "docs"
148	    if not docs.is_dir():
149	        return ["docs/: missing"]
150	    problems: list[str] = []
151	    tags = _tags(root)
152	    docstrings = _test_docstrings(root)
153	
154	    for path in docs.rglob("*"):
155	        if not path.is_file():
156	            continue
157	        text = _read(path)
158	        if "[[" not in text:
159	            continue
160	        rel = path.relative_to(root).as_posix()
161	        for match in WIKILINK.finditer(text):
162	            target = match.group(1).split("|", 1)[0].split("#", 1)[0].strip()
163	            if not _resolve(target, docs):
164	                problems.append(f"{rel}: wikilink {target} does not resolve")
165	
166	    version_notes: list[tuple[Path, str, dict[str, str], str]] = []
167	    for path in _notes(docs):
168	        rel = path.relative_to(root).as_posix()
169	        fm, body = frontmatter(_read(path))
170	        if fm is None:
171	            problems.append(f"{rel}: no frontmatter")
172	            continue
173	        kind = fm.get("type", "")
174	        if not kind:
175	            problems.append(f"{rel}: frontmatter has no type")
176	            continue
177	        if not (docs / "templates" / f"{kind}.md").is_file():
178	            problems.append(f"{rel}: type {kind} has no template docs/templates/{kind}.md")
179	            continue
180	        if kind == "seed":
181	            problems.extend(_seed_problems(path, rel, fm, body, root, tags, docstrings))
182	        elif kind == "version":
183	            version_notes.append((path, rel, fm, body))
184	
185	    for path, rel, fm, body in version_notes:
186	        for field in sorted(set(fm) - {"type"}):
187	            problems.append(f"{rel}: version note has field {field}")
188	        if not VERSION_NAME.match(path.name):
189	            problems.append(f"{rel}: version note is not named v<major>.<minor>.md")
190	    untagged = [(path, rel) for path, rel, _, _ in version_notes if path.stem not in tags]
191	    if len(untagged) > 1:
192	        for _, rel in untagged:
193	            problems.append(f"{rel}: at most one version note may not be a tag ({len(untagged)} are)")
194	    return problems

208	    for field in sorted(set(fm) - SEED_FIELDS):

210	    status = fm.get("status", "")
211	    if not status:

213	    if status not in STATUSES:

215	            f"{rel}: status {status} is not one of {', '.join(STATUSES)}"
216	        ]
217	    rank = STATUSES.index(status)
218	
219	    if not fm.get("summary", ""):

221	    value = fm.get("value", "")
222	    try:
223	        number = int(value)

228	    effort = fm.get("effort", "")
229	    if effort not in EFFORTS:

231	
232	    version = fm.get("version", "")
233	    if rank >= STATUSES.index("spec"):

236	        elif not (docs / "versions" / f"{version}.md").is_file():
